One instance ran on the platform (ryzen):\n\n- **dsh web on ryzen** \u2014 `dsh-web.service` (system unit, `User=bcloud`,\n  `DSH_HOME=/home/bcloud/.dsh`) ran `dsh web --no-open --host 127.0.0.1\n  --port 3080`; `dsh-lan-forward.service` (user unit, `~/.local/bin/dsh-lan-forward`)\n  re-exposed it on the box's current LAN IPv4 (`192.168.50.100:3080`, IP-agnostic).\n  The harness refused `--host 0.0.0.0` by design (\"would expose remote code\n  execution to the network\"), hence the loopback + SSH-forward split.\n\n# Runtime facts (historical)\n\n| Field | Value |\n|---|---|\n| ryzen UI port | 3080 (127.0.0.1 + LAN via `dsh-lan-forward`) |\n| ryzen service | `dsh-web.service` (system) |\n| LAN forward | `dsh-lan-forward.service` (user) |\n| version | 0.1.0-rc.7 (CLI), `dsh-oc-tui` 0.1.3 (TUI plugin) |\n| node prefix | v24.19.0 (dsh), v24.21.0 (dsh-oc-tui) |\n\n# MCP clients wired into the web profile\n\nThe web profile's user layer (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`, plus the\nglobal `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml`) loads `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` per\nserver; tools surfaced model-facing namespaced as `<serverName>_*`:\n\n| serverName | Transport | Target |\n|---|---|---|\n| `docs` | streamable-http | [Grounded Docs](/components/grounded-docs.md) `http://127.0.0.1:6280/mcp` (10 tools: scrape_docs, search_docs, \u2026) |\n| `proton-mail` | stdio | `proton-mail-bridge-mcp` (global patch layer) |\n\n# Credentials file (gotcha, fixed 2026-09-02)\n\n`~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` had to be a **flat mapping** `REF: string` \u2014\n`dsh-credentials-local` rejected nested/typed values (`version:` / `refs:`\nblocks crash the harness at boot with `must be a string`). The file was\nhand-written with `version: 1` + `refs:` on 2026-08-30 while the service ran\nsince 08-28, so the breakage only surfaced on restart; flattened to\n`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY: <sk-\u2026>` (the DeepSeek API key was the harness's model\ncredential).\n\n# Related\n\n- [strixhalo](/machines/strixhalo.md) \u2014 the inference machine; its dsh instance was removed 2026-09-03.\n- [DSH agent session memory (retired)](/references/dsh-agent-session-memory-2026-08.md) \u2014 the harness-side session notes, preserved.\n- [Grounded Docs](/components/grounded-docs.md) \u2014 docs MCP server wired in (still live).\n- [OpenDesign](/components/open-design.md) \u2014 sibling daemon on this host.", "components/fluxer-mcp": "# What it is\n\nAn MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that turns an AI agent into a\n**Fluxer community manager**. It wraps the Fluxer REST API and realtime\ngateway (OpenAPI spec at `api.fluxer.app/openapi.json`), exposing **46\ntools**.\n\nFluxer is a free, open-source, Discord-like chat platform \u2014 this is how\nagents run the 1bit.MONSTER guild.\n\n> \u26a0\ufe0f This bridge only reaches the **Fluxer platform**. The `auth_\u2026` \"Root Dev\n> Token\" in `~/Documents` is invalid on both surfaces (2026-08-28).\n\n# Capabilities\n\n- **Observe** \u2014 guilds, channels, members, roles, bans, invites, audit logs;\n  messages, profiles; message and member search.\n- **Communicate** \u2014 send/edit/delete/bulk-delete messages; reactions, pins,\n  typing.\n- **Moderate** \u2014 ban/unban, kick, timeout, nicknames, role management.\n- **Watch** \u2014 realtime gateway buffering events (`MESSAGE_CREATE`,\n  `GUILD_MEMBER_ADD`, `GUILD_BAN_ADD`, \u2026) drained via `fluxer_get_recent_events`.\n\n# Requirements & runtime\n\n- Node.js >= 22; a Fluxer bot token (or user session/OAuth2 bearer).\n- Build: `npm install && npm run build`; sources in `src/`, compiled to `dist/`.\n\n# Related\n\n- [Fluxer community reference](/references/fluxer-community.md) \u2014 the guild\n  it manages.\n- [Root MCP](/components/root-mcp.md) \u2014 the same pattern for the Root community.", "components/gh-auth-endpoint": "# What it is\n\nAn HTTP endpoint that mints **short-lived GitHub App installation tokens** (1 hour, revocable,\nApp-attributed). It exists so a machine or agent can obtain a token over a link instead of holding the\nApp private key \u2014 the same role `gh-app-token` plays on strixhalo, but reachable from anywhere.\n\n# Status: LIVE (verified 2026-09-12)\n\n`https://1bit-monster.pages.dev/gh-auth` \u2014 production deploy from `main`, verified end to end:\n\n| request | result |\n|---|---|\n| no bearer | `401 {\"error\":\"unauthorized\"}` |\n| wrong bearer | `401` |\n| correct bearer | mints a real installation token: `ghs_\u2026`, `expires_in=3599`, `account=1bit-MONSTER`, `installation=158270753` |\n| that token used with `gh` | 4 open PRs visible |\n| `?export=1` | `export GH_TOKEN='\u2026'` |\n\nTwo gates had to be cleared to get here, both worth remembering: **Scope Guard** requires committed\ntop-level paths to stay inside an allow-list (so the handler is committed under `site/` and `deploy.yml`\n*copies* it to `functions/` in the CI workspace \u2014 the repo gains no new top-level path, and a feature PR\nnever edits the guard that governs it), and **the merge queue only pends once every required check is\ngreen** \u2014 repeated main-merges reset the 20-minute C++ job and delayed it by an hour.\n\n# The link\n\n| route | auth | returns |\n|---|---|---|\n| `GET /gh-auth` | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` | `{token, expires_at, expires_in, account, installation_id}` |\n| `GET /gh-auth?export=1` | bearer | `export GH_TOKEN='\u2026'` (eval-friendly) |\n| `GET /gh-auth/healthz` | none | `{ok, configured, account}` \u2014 no secrets. **Note**: a single-file function is routed at exactly `/gh-auth`; `healthz` is matched inside the handler by suffix, but the *path* `/gh-auth/healthz` is a different route and 404s. Use `/gh-auth` and read `configured`, or add `functions/gh-auth/healthz.js`. |\n\n```\neval \"$(curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOK\" https://1bit.monster/gh-auth?export=1)\"\ngh pr list -R 1bit-MONSTER/1bit-MONSTER --state open\n```\n\nThe caller bearer lives in the vault: `~/Documents/gh auth worker token.txt` (sha256 prefix\n`a2bdbf85`), mirrored as the repo secret `GH_AUTH_WORKER_TOKEN`.\n\n# Deployment facts learned the hard way\n\n1. **Pages Functions are compiled from the project root, not from inside the upload directory.**\n   `site/functions/**.js` is uploaded as *static assets* (the deploy log shows file uploads and no\n   compile step); even the deployment's own URL 404s them. The handler therefore lives at\n   `functions/gh-auth.js` in the repo root, and `deploy.yml` gained `functions/**` in its push paths \u2014\n   without that, changing the handler would not trigger a deploy.\n2. **`1bit.monster` is served by GitHub Pages**, not by the Cloudflare Pages project (the site's 404 page\n   says so in its own comment, and the repo carries a `CNAME`). So a Cloudflare Function can only answer\n   on the Pages hosts \u2014 `https://1bit-monster.pages.dev/gh-auth` (production alias) or a\n   `<hash>.1bit-monster.pages.dev` deployment URL. A prettier host needs a custom domain attached to the\n   Pages project (e.g. `gh.1bit.monster`).\n3. **Production and preview environments have separate secrets.** A branch dispatch is a *preview*\n   deployment, so it does not see secrets set for production: the function answers\n   `{\"error\":\"not configured (AUTH_TOKEN secret missing)\"}` there. That is also the smoke test that the\n   function is alive \u2014 it returns JSON rather than the static 404.\n4. **Pre-existing and still broken:** `site/functions/[[path]].js` (SEO verification files) and\n   `site/functions/api/checkout.js` (store checkout) sit in the same non-compiled location, i.e. they have\n   never been served either. Moving them is a behaviour change and was deliberately left out of the\n   routing fix.\n\n# Where it lives, and why there\n\n`site/functions/gh-auth.js` in the engine repo (`1bit-MONSTER/1bit-MONSTER`, which is what\n`bong-water-water-bong/1bit-systems` redirects to \u2014 the repo was renamed, so `~/1bit-systems` is an old\ncheckout of the same repo). It is a **Pages Function**, not a standalone Worker, and that is a\ndeliberate consequence of the authorization in place:\n\n* the repo's `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` covers **Pages** \u2014 the site deploys with it;\n* it does **not** cover **Workers Scripts**: `wrangler deploy` fails with\n  `Authentication error [code: 10000] \u2014 Failed to automatically retrieve account IDs`;\n* Pages Functions run on the same runtime, so the endpoint rides the site deploy the token can already do.\n\nThe standalone Worker variant (`workers/gh-auth/**` + `deploy-gh-auth.yml`) is preserved in the history of\nbranch `feat/gh-auth-worker` for the day a Workers-scoped token exists; it is not deployed.\n\n**Deploy path**: `deploy.yml` sets `APP_ID` / `APP_PRIVATE_KEY` / `AUTH_TOKEN` as **Pages project secrets**\n(from the same repo secrets) and then deploys the site \u2014 so the function's configuration travels with the\nsite, and no secret is ever a repo file. A branch dispatch deploys a *preview*; only a deploy from `main`\nupdates the production aliases (`1bit.monster`, `1bit-monster.pages.dev`).\n\n# Verification\n\n`site/functions/gh-auth.test.mjs` drives the real handler against the **real** GitHub API (no mocks, 10\nchecks: mint, installation-token prefix, expiry, cache reuse, 401 wrong bearer, 401 missing bearer, 405\nmethod, export route, healthz leaks nothing, key never echoed). It runs in CI via\n`gh-auth-verify.yml` on every PR touching the path, and it already earned its keep: it caught that GitHub\nhands App keys out as **PKCS#1**, which WebCrypto cannot import \u2014 the handler now wraps PKCS#1 in PKCS#8\nitself rather than mutating a secret five other workflows also use.\n\n# Security notes\n\nBearer required (constant-time compare) or 401 with no minting; the key is never returned or logged;\nresponses are `no-store`; tokens cannot exceed the installation. Recommended second layer: Cloudflare\nAccess in front, and/or rotate the bearer (a config change \u2014 the handler is deliberately small).\n\n# Related\n\n* [Credential vault](/references/index.md) \u2014 the bearer, and the App's id/installation (App\n  `1bit-traffic-bot`, installation `158270753`, 5 repos) via the existing `gh-app-token` helper.\n* [Chess arg-delivery defect](/references/chess-arg-delivery-defect.md) \u2014 unrelated work that used the\n  same App to drive `gh` from ryzen.", "components/grounded-docs": "# What it is\n\n**Grounded Docs** (`@arabold/docs-mcp-server`, MIT, Node \u226522) is the\nopen-source alternative to Context7 / Nia / Ref.Tools: it fetches official\ndocs from websites, GitHub, npm, PyPI, and local folders **on demand**, and\nserves version-specific, searchable documentation to coding agents over\nMCP. Runs fully locally; no cloud dependency.\n\n# Deployment (ryzen, docker compose)\n\nRepo: `~/projects/docs-mcp-server` (`docker-compose.yml` \u2014 3 services from\n`ghcr.io/arabold/docs-mcp-server:latest`):\n\n| Service | Container | Port | Role |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| worker | `docs-mcp-worker` | 8080 (internal) | scrapes/indexes docs; health-gated |\n| mcp | `docs-mcp-server` | **6280** | MCP endpoint (streamable HTTP + SSE) |\n| web | `docs-mcp-web` | **6281** | browser management UI |\n\nOps: `cd ~/projects/docs-mcp-server && docker compose up -d --force-recreate`.\nThe compose file carries a local patch: `extra_hosts: host.docker.internal:host-gateway`\non all three services (Linux Docker does not resolve it otherwise).\n\n# Embeddings \u2014 wired to the 1bit engine (not Ollama/OpenAI)\n\n`~/.env` (in the repo) points embeddings at the engine's embed-server on\nstrixhalo through a persistent SSH tunnel:\n\n```\nDOCS_MCP_EMBEDDING_MODEL=openai:nomic-embed-text-v1-GGUF\nOPENAI_API_KEY=engine\nOPENAI_API_BASE=http://host.docker.internal:8099/v1\n```\n\n- strixhalo embed-server: `build/1bit unified --lemonade --port 8088` +\n  cache `~/.cache/lemonade-seo` (model `nomic-embed-text-v1-GGUF`, 768-d,\n  labelled `embeddings` \u2192 llama-server `--embeddings`). See\n  [strixhalo access points](/references/strixhalo-access-points.md).\n- Tunnel: `docs-mcp-engine-tunnel.service` (systemd user) \u2014 ryzen\n  `0.0.0.0:8099` \u2192 strixhalo `127.0.0.1:8088`.\n- ufw: `allow from 172.16.0.0/12 to any port 8099 proto tcp` (container\u2192host).\n\nGotchas learned: lemonade only enables `--embeddings` for\n`ModelType::EMBEDDING` models (chat GGUFs \u2192 501); llama-server physical\nbatch 512 \u2192 `--ubatch-size 2048` in config; host.docker.internal needs the\n`extra_hosts` patch; ufw blocks container\u2192host on Docker.\n\n# Usage\n\n```bash\n# CLI (inside the worker container, same image)\ndocker exec docs-mcp-worker node dist/index.js scrape <name> <url>\ndocker exec docs-mcp-worker node dist/index.js search <name> \"<query>\"\ndocker exec docs-mcp-worker node dist/index.js list\ndocker exec docs-mcp-worker node dist/index.js refresh <name>   # incremental re-scrape\n```\n\n- MCP: point Claude/Cursor at `http://<ryzen>:6280/mcp` (streamable HTTP).\n- MCP: wired into the [DeepSeek Harness](/components/dsh.md) web profile\n  (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`, `serverName: docs`) \u2014 harness\n  agents call `docs_*` tools (`scrape_docs`, `search_docs`, \u2026).\n- Web UI: `http://<ryzen>:6281/`.\n\n# Indexed libraries (2026-09-02)\n\n| Library | Source | Docs / URLs |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1bit-engine | github.com/1bit-MONSTER/1bit-MONSTER | 27,800 / 999 |\n| mcp-ts-sdk | github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk | 12,588 / 611 |\n| zod | zod.dev | 4,105 / 100 |\n| fastapi | fastapi.tiangolo.com | 2,669 / 200 |\n| nextjs | nextjs.org/docs | 1,438 / 250 |\n| lemonade | lemonade-server.ai/docs | 508 / 66 |\n| react | react.dev/reference/react | 459 / 49 |\n| htmlparser2 | github.com/fb55/htmlparser2 | 476 / 29 |\n\nAdd more with `scrape <name> <url>` (sites: `--max-pages N`; hash-routed SPA\nneed `--preserve-hashes`). `refresh <name>` re-scrapes changed pages.\n\n# Embedding sizing gotchas (fixed 2026-09-02)\n\n- Grounded Docs batches embeddings by **chars** (`embeddings.batchChars` in\n  the config volume `/config/docs-mcp-server/config.yaml`, **not** an env\n  override despite .env.example; default 50_000).\n- The 1bit engine's llama-server rejected requests over its ubatch:\n  `500 input (N tokens) is too large... current batch size: 2048`. Fixed\n  engine-side: `llamacpp.args = \"--ubatch-size 4096 --batch-size 4096\"` in\n  `~/.cache/lemonade-seo/config.json` on strixhalo (embed-server.service).\n  With that, batchChars 7000 + ubatch 4096 \u2192 ~0 failures.\n- Known scraper crash: `AssertionError Parser.finish` (undici HTTP parser)\n  on some GitHub repos (lemonade-sdk/lemonade) \u2014 use the project's docs\n  website instead.\n\n# Related\n\n- [1bit engine](/components/1bit-engine.md) \u2014 embeddings backend\n- [Context7](/components/context7.md) \u2014 the hosted service this replaces\n- [Port map](/references/ports.md)", "components/jarvis": "# What it is\n\nJARVIS is the reference application that proves the [engine](/components/1bit-engine.md):\n\n```\nmic \u2192 VAD \u2192 STT (libwhisper) \u2192 LLM (engine) \u2192 TTS (piper) \u2192 speaker\n```\n\nEvery stage is **in-process, pure C++**, and the LLM stage runs on any\nengine backend \u2014 NPU, GPU, CPU.\n\n# JARVIS v2 (rebuild 2026-08-06)\n\nv1 was a C++ port of a deleted Python package that carried the whole\ndeleted product stack (auth, billing, usage, beacon, personas, RAG, an\nHTTP agent server). v2 gutted all of it:\n\n- **One process** \u2014 in-process `BackendManager`; the engine IS the app.\n- **Pure C++** \u2014 only subprocesses are `arecord`, `aplay`, `piper`.\n- **Thin** \u2014 `tools/jarvis/` is 9 files, ~1300 lines.\n\n# Default experience: the Zyphra stack\n\nWithout `--model`, JARVIS picks the first Zyphra model in the weights dir\n(preference: ZAYA1-8B \u2192 ZAYA1-74B \u2192 BlackMamba-2.8B \u2192 BlackMamba-1.5B \u2192\nZamba2-7B/2.7B/1.2B \u2192 ZR1-1.5B). `--model <any>` bypasses it. Install via\n`bash install.sh --with-jarvis` \u2192 `jarvis` launcher + `~/.config/1bit/jarvis.env`\n(+ optional systemd user unit at login).\n\n# Build & run\n\n```bash\ncmake --build build --target jarvis_app          # build/jarvis\n./build/1bit jarvis --model \"Qwen3-0.6B\" --text   # text chat\n./build/1bit jarvis --model \"Qwen3-0.6B\" \\\n    --whisper models/whisper-tiny.gguf \\\n    --piper-model ~/piper/en_US-lessac-medium.onnx   # voice\n```\n\nFlags: `--model` (required), `--weights-dir`, `--text`, `--whisper`,\n`--piper`/`--piper-model`, `--mic DEVICE`, `--system`, `--max-tokens`.\n\n# Status (honest)\n\n| Stage | Status |\n|---|---|\n| VAD | \u2705 energy-based, 20 ms frames, lookback/ramp-down |\n| LLM | \u2705 in-process, any backend, last-6-turns history; default Zyphra |\n| TTS | \u2705 piper (fork/exec, 22050 Hz); codec voice = P2 |\n| STT | \u2705 GPU-accelerated (`src/whisper_hip.hip`; `WHISPER_GPU=0` forces scalar) |\n| Barge-in | \ud83d\udd32 utterances during reply are dropped (P1) |\n\n# Roadmap\n\n- P1: STT on engine backends (NPU); sentence-streaming TTS; barge-in.\n- P2: stock codec voice via ONNX (no training, no voice packs); native\n  ALSA audio (`snd_pcm` instead of `arecord`/`aplay` pipes).\n\n# Related\n\n- [1bit engine](/components/1bit-engine.md)\n- [Model families](/references/model-families.md) \u2014 the Zyphra stack", "components/kernel-lab": "# What it is\n\nA working pipeline for **writing GPU kernels by hand in raw AMDGCN assembly**\nand running them on strixhalo's Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), mirroring the\nNetra-kernel approach (hand-written ISA \u2192 code object \u2192 C ABI/HSA bridge).\n\nMirrored locally at `~/projects/kernel-lab/vecadd/`. Everything builds and\nruns on strixhalo with the TheRock toolchain.\n\n# The pipeline (how hand-writing works)\n\n```\nHIP source  \u2192  clang \u2192 AMDGCN ISA (.s)  \u2192  amdclang -shared \u2192 ET_DYN .hsaco\n                                                        \u2193\n    HSA API: code object reader \u2192 executable \u2192 \"<name>.kd\" symbol\n                                                        \u2193\n    hand-rolled AQL dispatch packet (64-byte)  \u2192  GPU waves\n```\n\nA hand-written kernel = **the ISA in `.s` + the kernel descriptor\n(`.amdhsa_kernel` directives) + the `.amdgpu_metadata` YAML** (which becomes\nthe `.note` section the loader parses). Plus hand-rolling the dispatch.\n\n# Artifacts (strixhalo:~/kernel-lab/vecadd/)\n\n| File | What |\n|---|---|\n| `vecadd_hand.s` | 18-instruction hand-written vecadd (2 floats/thread) \u2014 the ABI/demo baseline |\n| `hsa_launch.cpp` | Generic HSA loader + AQL dispatcher (reusable harness) |\n| `tq2_gemv.s` | Hand-written TQ2_0_g128 ternary GEMV (6912\u00d76912) |\n| `tq2_launch.cpp` | TQ2 bench: same seed as the HIP baseline, CPU fp32 reference, timing |\n| `bench_tq2_baseline.cpp` | HIP baseline (bonsai_tq2_gemv.hip, the librocm_cpp.so kernel source) |\n| `README.md` | Build/run commands + retained experiments |\n\n# TQ2 GEMV results (2026-08-26)\n\nSame data (seed 1234), same CPU reference, same harness:\n\n| | correctness | latency | effective BW |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| HIP kernel (clang -O3, in librocm_cpp.so) | 0/6912, err 0.0503 | **0.074 ms** | **172 GB/s** |\n| Hand-written AMDGCN | 0/6912, err 0.0503 | 0.182 ms | 71 GB/s |\n\nCorrect \u2014 but the compiler's kernel is ~2.4\u00d7 faster. **Lesson: hand-writing\nis for measuring/teaching and for gaps the compiler can't reach; re-deriving\nstandard kernels by hand rarely beats clang -O3.**\n\n# Retained experiments (did not pass promotion)\n\nDocumented in the README, Netra-style (\"positive measurements and\nexperiments that did not pass promotion gates\"):\n\n1. **`v_dot2_f32_f16` computes 0 on gfx1151** \u2014 verified in a 5-line HIP\n   micro-test (assembles, executes, silently returns 0). The fp16-LUT +\n   dot2 decode path was abandoned.\n2. **Software-pipelined double-buffer** \u2014 never reached correctness on this\n   target (arg-offset mismatch, codegen register aliasing, OOB prefetch,\n   kernarg overflow). Complexity exceeded the gain.\n3. **`hipModuleLoad` / `hipModuleLoadData` segfault** on external code\n   objects in this TheRock runtime \u2014 use the HSA API directly.\n\n# Verified\n\nvecadd: `PASS 16,777,216 elements` on the real GPU. TQ2: `0/6912 mismatches\nvs CPU ref` at 6912\u00d76912. See also [the gfx1151 findings](/references/amdgcn-gfx1151.md).", "components/lemonade-server": "# What it is\n\n**Lemonade Server** ([lemonade-server.ai](https://lemonade-server.ai/docs/),\n[lemonade-sdk/lemonade](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/lemonade)) is AMD's\nproject \"to make the world of local AI simple\": a CLI, a server, a desktop\napp, and a web UI that serve models through standard APIs \u2014 **OpenAI\ncompatible**, **Ollama compatible**, **Anthropic compatible**, and\nllama.cpp-specific endpoints. Apache 2.0, \u00a9 2026 AMD.\n\n- Backends it can drive: llama.cpp, vLLM, Moonshine, and (via routing)\n  the 1bit NPU/GPU engines.\n- App integrations: Claude Code, AnythingLLM, CodeGPT, Continue, LangChain,\n  Open WebUI, and more.\n- Ships a portable, embeddable binary; exposes an MCP server.\n\n# Relationship to the 1bit engine (embedded fork, no wrappers)\n\nThe [1bit engine](/components/1bit-engine.md) **embeds a vendored fork of\nthe Lemonade SDK** at `third_party/lemonade` (pinned v11.7.0 / `2b6a7d77`,\nlocally patched for embeddability) and **compiles its server core into the\nsame binary** (object library linked into `build/1bit`) \u2014 no FFI, no\nwrappers, both sides C++. The engine therefore **supports the entire\nLemonade SDK surface**: all 14 backends, the RoutingPolicyEngine, and the\nfull API set via `unified_server --lemonade`. No separate Lemonade install\nis needed for engine use; the standalone server is only for running\nLemonade directly. See the [1bit engine](/components/1bit-engine.md) for\nthe vendoring details.\n\n# 1bit engine integration (OpenAI-compatible routing)\n\nBoth sides speak the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` API, so\nLemonade routes omni-modal requests to the 1bit engines as a sub-process or\nremote server (`1bit-halo-server` on :8180 \u2014 NPU engine; the ZINC GPU\nengine). From the engine's [Lemonade compatibility doc](https://github.com/1bit-MONSTER/1bit-MONSTER/blob/main/docs/guides/Lemonade-Compat.md):\n\n```yaml\n# lemonade config.yaml\nmodels:\n  - name: qwen3-npu\n    server:\n      url: http://127.0.0.1:9090   # FLM proxy or 1bit-halo-server\n      type: openai\n```\n\n- **`*_bin` config keys** (Lemonade \u2265 v10.3, PR #1713) \u2014 every backend\n  binary accepts `builtin` / `latest` / version tag / local path; the 1bit\n  packaging supplies `ryzenai.server_bin` as `latest` or a pinned tag.\n- **First-party contribution** \u2014 `bong-water-water-bong` is a listed\n  contributor in Lemonade v10.9.0 (test/documentation, PR #2447).\n- **flm sync** \u2014 the [FastFlowLM](/playbooks/build-engine.md) binary the 1bit\n  NPU backend spawns is \"the same binary Lemonade Server tracks and stays in\n  sync with\".\n- **MCP** \u2014 both projects expose MCP servers.\n\n# Version compatibility (from the engine repo)\n\n| 1bit.systems | Lemonade | Status |\n|---|---|---|\n| v2026.08+ | v11.8.0 | \u2705 Vendored & embedded (built + smoke-tested 2026-08-26; ds4 backend, model register/options, download resume) |\n| v2026.07+ | v10.9.0 | \u2705 Verified (Jul 2026) |\n| v2026.04+ | v10.3 | \u2705 Compatible (API stable) |\n| v2026.04+ | v10.0+ | \u2705 Basic chat |\n\n# v11.8.0 known issue \u2014 config/model path migration\n\nUpstream **11.8.0** moved where lemond searches for config and models, with an\nauto-migration that **fails on the Ubuntu PPA and Arch installers** (other\nplatforms OK). Tracked in\n[lemonade-sdk/lemonade#3394](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/lemonade/issues/3394);\nthe Ubuntu PPA build was yanked; hotfix (11.8.1) pending.\n\n- New layout: config \u2192 `/var/lib/lemonade/`, cache \u2192 `/var/cache/lemonade/`,\n  HF cache \u2192 `/var/cache/huggingface` (was `/var/lib/lemonade/.cache/\u2026`).\n- Manual fix (only if you must; upstream recommends waiting for 11.8.1):\n\n  ```bash\n  sudo mv /var/lib/lemonade/.cache/lemonade/config.json /var/lib/lemonade/\n  sudo mv /var/lib/lemonade/.cache/lemonade/recipe_options.json /var/lib/lemonade/\n  sudo mv /var/lib/lemonade/.cache/lemonade/user_models.json /var/lib/lemonade/\n  sudo mkdir /var/cache/lemonade\n  sudo mv /var/lib/lemonade/.cache/lemonade/bin /var/cache/lemonade/bin\n  sudo mv /var/lib/lemonade/.cache/huggingface /var/cache/huggingface\n  sudo chown -R lemonade:lemonade /var/lib/lemonade /var/cache/lemonade /var/cache/huggingface\n  ```\n\n- If you moved models to `/var/cache/huggingface` yourself, set\n  `HF_HOME=/var/cache/huggingface` **before** upgrading to 11.8.1.\n- API keys after manual migration go in `/etc/default/lemond`.\n- Community discussion: Lemonade Discord thread \"Default paths changing\"\n  (see [Discord access](/references/discord-access.md)).\n\n# Related\n\n- [1bit engine](/components/1bit-engine.md)\n- [Build the engine](/playbooks/build-engine.md) \u2014 TheRock/flm discovery\n  (`~/.cache/lemonade/bin/therock` is a TheRock discovery path)", "components/open-design": "# What it is\n\nThe OpenDesign daemon, self-hosted locally (systemd service\n`open-design.service`, `User=bcloud`). It provides the OpenDesign MCP\nsurface \u2014 project management, artifact generation runs, skills/plugins, and\nthe Studio/Preview browser delivery.\n\n# Runtime facts\n\n| Field | Value |\n|---|---|\n| Working directory | `/opt/open-design` |\n| Exec | `node /opt/open-design/apps/daemon/dist/cli.js --no-open` |\n| Port | **7456** (0.0.0.0) |\n| Service | `open-design.service` (system) |\n\n# Related\n\n- [dsh](/components/dsh.md) \u2014 sibling daemon (web UI) on this host.\n- [Zyphra proxy](/components/zyphra-proxy.md) \u2014 sibling agent-infra service.", "components/proton-bridge": "# What it is\n\nThe Proton Bridge running locally on [ryzen](/machines/ryzen.md). It exposes\nthe Proton account `bcloud@1bit.monster` over IMAP/SMTP on loopback so mail\ncan be read, searched, summarized, replied to, forwarded, and sent \u2014 without\nthe Proton cloud API.\n\n# Runtime facts\n\n| Field | Value |\n|---|---|\n| SMTP | 127.0.0.1:1025 |\n| IMAP | 127.0.0.1:1143 |\n| Account | bcloud@1bit.monster |\n\n# Notes\n\n- Loopback-only; useful for agents (e.g. the proton-mail skill) and mail\n  tooling on this host.", "components/rocm-cpp": "# What it is\n\n`librocm_cpp.so` \u2014 the shared library exposing the engine's **C API to the\nHIP/ROCm GPU backends** (\"we made our own kernels\"). `backend_factory.cpp`\ndlopens it at runtime for `create_hip_backend` and `create_vulkan_backend`;\nthe `1bit` binary links it.\n\n**Not dusty**: rebuilt 2026-08-25 (yesterday), and the `kernels/` directory\n(47 HIP kernels + 5 Vulkan shaders) is its evolution.\n\n# Kernel inventory (the \"our own\" stack)\n\n| Group | Kernels (kernels/*.hip) |\n|---|---|\n| MoE | `zaya_persistent_moe` (single grid, 40 layers), `zaya_moe_wmma_batched`, `zaya_moe_tiled_gemv`, `zaya_moe_expert_ffn`, `zaya_moe_batch_union`, `zaya_moe_ternary_gemv` |\n| GEMM/GEMV | `wmma_i8_gemv`, `zaya_gemv_bf16`, `fused_qkv_gemv`, `fused_norm_gemv`, `lm_head_fused`, ternary family (`ternary_gemv_wmma`, `_sherry`, `_phase5_dot4`, `_tq1_halo`), `iq_gemv`, `q4k_gemv`, `bitnet_gguf_gemv`, `bonsai_q1_gemv_soa`, `twla_*`, `fp8_wmma_gemv` |\n| Attention | `zaya_cca_attn`, `zaya_batch_v_attn`, `deepseek_mla`, `vitallm_sparse_attn` |\n| Quant/KV | `oscar_quant`, `turboquant_kv`, `rotorquant_pack` |\n| NPU (XDNA) | DPU kernels (`engine/npu/kernel/stq_aiesim`, `tq2_aiesim`), AIE microkernels (research ws01\u2013ws04), hybrid NPU\u2194GPU overlap |\n\nTargets the **detected** GPU via TheRock clang: `CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES` comes from `scripts/detect-gfx-targets.sh` (`gfx1151` on Strix Halo, `gfx1036;gfx1201` on ryzen). It is no longer hardcoded to `gfx1151`.\nThe old standalone era (`bitnet_decode`, 113 tok/s Bonsai-1.7B,\nbandwidth-bound at ~50 GB/s) is archived in `docs/archive/HANDOFF-ROCM-GPU.md`.\n\n# Relationship to Netra\n\nNetra writes raw AMDGCN assembly for gfx950/gfx1151 + SGLang bridges; we\nwrite HIP + Vulkan + XDNA DPU kernels inside one C++23 binary. Same problems\n(kernel-level optimization, fused GDN, launch amortization), different\nlayers and targets. See [Netra benchmark methodology](/references/netra-benchmark.md)\nand the [kernel lab](/components/kernel-lab.md) for the hand-written layer.\n\n# Verified\n\n2026-08-26: TQ2 GEMV benchmark run against the lib's kernel source\n(`bonsai_tq2_gemv.hip`, exported as `bonsai_tq2_gemv_launch`) \u2014 0/6912 vs\nCPU ref, 0.074 ms at 6912\u00d76912.", "components/root-bot": "# \u26d4 Status \u2014 DECOMMISSIONED (confirmed by human:bcloud, 2026-09-06)\n\nNot running (verified in the 2026-09-06 post-reboot full systems check: no\ndocker container/image, no `:8765`, no process; sources idle since\n2026-08-20). Historical record; delete the page on request.\n\n# What it is\n\n`root-mcp` \u2014 a Model Context Protocol server in the 1bit-monster workspace\nthat gives AI agents direct access to the Root community (the same surface\nthe [Root bot](/components/root-bot.md) exposes over HTTP, but as typed MCP\ntools).\n\n# Status\n\n- Workspace scaffold exists at `/home/bcloud/1bit-monster/root-mcp` (`src/`\n  only) \u2014 early-stage, no published package ever shipped.\n- Never ran as a docker container on [ryzen](/machines/ryzen.md) (verified\n  2026-09-06 \u2014 no image, no container).\n\n# Relationship\n\n- [Root bot](/components/root-bot.md) \u2014 runtime bridge, HTTP control API\n  (also decommissioned).\n- [Fluxer MCP](/components/fluxer-mcp.md) \u2014 the same pattern, but for the\n  Fluxer guild instead of the Root community.", "components/strixhalo-mcp": "# What it is\n\nAn MCP server (TS, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.30, zod 4) exposing the\n**local inference stack on [strixhalo](/machines/strixhalo.md)** as agent\ntools \u2014 the free, on-prem counterpart to cloud providers. ~8 tok/s, TTFT ~2.7\u20133 s) |\n| `strixhalo_embed` | nomic-embed-text-v1-GGUF (768-d) \u2014 dim/count stats |\n| `strixhalo_embed_vectors` | Same, raw vectors for agent-side similarity/RAG |\n\nPlus `strixhalo_status` (extension-level bridge status; fluxer pattern).\n\n# Topology & tunnels\n\n| Hop | Port (ryzen) | \u2192 strixhalo | Service | Component |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| FastFlowLM chat | `127.0.0.1:8090` | `127.0.0.1:8098` | `strixhalo-chat-tunnel.service` (user, enabled 2026-09-06) | `flm-35b.service` (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, OpenAI-compat) |\n| 1bit/lemonade embed | `0.0.0.0:8099` | `127.0.0.1:8088` | `docs-mcp-engine-tunnel.service` (shared with [Grounded Docs](/components/grounded-docs.md)) | `embed-server.service` (nomic-embed-text-v1, 768-d) |\n\nBoth backends bind loopback on strixhalo; the SSH tunnels are the only path.\nThe MCP server itself runs on ryzen (stdio child of the pi extension) and\ntalks OpenAI-compatible HTTP to the tunneled ports.\n\n# Config\n\nEnv with working local defaults: `STRIXHALO_CHAT_BASE_URL`\n(`http://127.0.0.1:8090/v1`), `STRIXHALO_CHAT_MODEL`\n(`qwen3.6-moe:35b-a3b`), `STRIXHALO_EMBED_BASE_URL`\n(`http://127.0.0.1:8099/v1`), `STRIXHALO_EMBED_MODEL`\n(`nomic-embed-text-v1-GGUF`), `STRIXHALO_TIMEOUT_MS` (`300000`).\n\n# Gotchas\n\n- Only `qwen3.6-moe:35b-a3b` is **resident** on the chat server; the other\n  35 FastFlowLM catalog ids are known-but-not-loaded (requesting one may\n  trigger a download). Pass an explicit `model` only for the 35B.\n- Embed catalog = GGUF files registered from `~/models` (loadable on demand\n  by llama.cpp); `nomic-embed-text-v1-GGUF` is the embeddings model\n  (`ModelType::EMBEDDING` \u2192 `--embeddings`; chat GGUFs 501 on /v1/embeddings).\n- NPU decode ~8 tok/s \u2192 keep `max_tokens` modest (default 256).\n- Chat tunnel binds loopback only; embed tunnel binds `0.0.0.0` (pre-existing,\n  container\u2192host ufw rule from Grounded Docs).\n\n# Verification\n\n`node scripts/smoke.mjs` (2026-09-06, 8/8 against live tunnels): initialize \u2192\ntools/list (5) \u2192 health (both reachable, hot models correct) \u2192 list_models\n(36 chat ids incl. 35B; 19 embed ids incl. nomic) \u2192 embed (dim 768) \u2192 chat\n(`\"pong\"`, TTFT 2.73 s). API surfaces re-verified live: FastFlowLM\n`/v1/chat/completions` usage block carries `prefill_duration_ttft` +\n`decoding_speed_tps`; lemonade `/v1/embeddings` returns 768-d vectors.\n\n# Related\n\n- [Fluxer MCP](/components/fluxer-mcp.md) / [Discord MCP](/components/discord-mcp.md) \u2014 sibling bridge pattern (pi extension spawns stdio MCP server)\n- [Zyphra proxy](/components/zyphra-proxy.md) + zyphra-cloud extension \u2014 the cloud side of agent LLM access\n- [1bit engine](/components/1bit-engine.md), [Lemonade Server](/components/lemonade-server.md), [FastFlowLM](/playbooks/build-engine.md) \u2014 the backends being exposed\n- [strixhalo](/machines/strixhalo.md) + [access points](/references/strixhalo-access-points.md) \u2014 host inventory\n- [Port map](/references/ports.md) \u2014 8090 added 2026-09-06", "components/traffic-report": "# What it is\n\n`traffic-report` is a single command that fetches **today's + 14-day\ntraffic from both platforms at once**:\n\n* **GitHub** \u2014 views & clones for every repo under the user account\n  (`bong-water-water-bong`) **and** the `1bit-MONSTER` org, via the local\n  `gh` CLI against the Traffic API (parallel, ~10 s).\n* **Cloudflare** \u2014 1bit.monster zone edge analytics (requests/page views\n  per day) + RUM Web Analytics (visits, top pages, referrers, attribution),\n  by triggering the existing `analytics.yml` \"Site Analytics\" workflow on\n  `1bit-MONSTER/1bit-MONSTER` and extracting the report from the run log\n  (~1\u20132 min, dominated by runner spin-up).\n\n# Installations on this host\n\n| Piece | Where |\n|---|---|\n| script | `~/.local/bin/traffic-report` |\n| GH table filter | `~/.local/lib/traffic-report/gh-table.py` |\n| CF log extractor | `~/.local/lib/traffic-report/cf-extract.py` |\n\n# Usage\n\n```bash\ntraffic-report          # GitHub + Cloudflare (everything)\ntraffic-report --gh     # GitHub only\ntraffic-report --cf     # Cloudflare only\ntraffic-report --json   # GitHub part as JSON\n```\n\nEnv overrides: `GH_TRAFFIC_OWNER` (default `bong-water-water-bong`),\n`GH_TRAFFIC_ORG` (default `1bit-MONSTER`), `CF_WORKFLOW_REPO` (default\n`1bit-MONSTER/1bit-MONSTER`).\n\n# Why Cloudflare goes through a workflow\n\nThe local wrangler OAuth state (`~/.config/.wrangler/config/default.toml`)\nexpired 2026-08-25 and its refresh token was **revoked** (`invalid_grant` on\n`dash.cloudflare.com/oauth2/token`), so there is no usable Cloudflare token\non this host. The API tokens (`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `CLOUDFLARE_WA_TOKEN`,\n`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`) exist only as GitHub Actions secrets on\n`1bit-MONSTER/1bit-MONSTER`. The workflow trigger + log pull is therefore the\nlocal read path; the `gh` account has admin on the org, so the trigger works.\n\n# Data sources & caveats\n\n| Source | API | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| GitHub views/clones | `repos/{owner}/{repo}/traffic/{views,clones}` | 14 **complete** days ending **yesterday** \u2014 the window never carries today, and it **rolls over during the UTC day**: measured 2026-09-12, a 02:46 UTC call still returned the previous window (newest day = D-2) while a 13:23 UTC call returned the current one (newest day = D-1). Never label the newest row \"Today\" |\n| CF zone edge | GraphQL `httpRequests1dGroups` (zone `1bit.monster`, id `786c1cd9\u2026`) | per-day requests + pageViews; today's row fills in as the day progresses |\n| CF RUM | GraphQL `rumPageloadEventsAdaptiveGroups` (site token `87349337\u2026`, read from `site/analytics.js`) | 7-day window; visits, top pages, referrers, `/s/\u2026` share attribution |\n\nTraffic API requires push-level access per repo; the `gh` account qualifies\nfor both the user and org repos.\n\n# Observed baseline (2026-08-27)\n\n* GitHub 14d: `1bit-MONSTER/1bit-MONSTER` **22,183 clones / 385 unique,\n  1,924 views / 84 unique** (the traffic driver; the user's fork only ~50\n  clones); next: `mlir-aie` 1,559, `llama.cpp` 1,425, `lemonade` 820.\n* Cloudflare zone: 2026-08-25 805 req / 455 pv; 08-26 1,141 req / 265 pv;\n  08-27 212 req / 111 pv (refreshed ~18:10 UTC via workflow trigger).\n* RUM (7d): 19 visits \u2014 top page `/` (18); referrers 17 direct, 1 google,\n  1 github. No beacon token drift (site token `87349337\u2026` valid).\n* Deployments API shows Pages deployments stuck at stage `queued` \u2014\n  **verified cosmetic 2026-08-27**: wrangler direct-upload deploys never\n  advance the API stage (no build pipeline runs) but are live; preview URL\n  was byte-identical to 1bit.monster and the latest post\n  (`/1bit-post-lemonade-v1180.html`) returned 200.\n\n# Verified\n\nEnd-to-end run on 2026-08-27 produced both sections correctly; the\nworkflow-trigger path refreshes CF numbers vs the scheduled 06:00 UTC run\n(zone today went 18 req \u2192 144 req between the 01:32 and 12:10 runs).", "components/zyphra-proxy": "# What it is\n\nA translation proxy that lets Claude Code talk to **Zyphra Cloud** through\nthe Anthropic Messages API shape, plus a balance monitor. The upstream API\nsurface is documented in the [Zyphra Cloud API](/references/zyphra-cloud-api.md)\nreference (chat completions, TTS, voice clones, EEG, models, billing).\n\n# Pieces\n\n- `proxy.mjs` \u2014 node translation proxy, listens on `127.0.0.1:8787`.\n- `balance-monitor.mjs` \u2014 checks the Zyphra Cloud balance every 15 minutes.\n\n# Runtime facts\n\n| Field | Value |\n|---|---|\n| Proxy port | 8787 (127.0.0.1) |\n| proxy service | `zyphra-proxy.service` (user) |\n| monitor service | `zyphra-balance-monitor.service` + `.timer` (user, 15 min) |\n| Exec | `node /home/bcloud/.claude/zyphra-proxy/proxy.mjs` |\n\n# Related\n\n- [OpenDesign](/components/open-design.md) and [dsh](/components/dsh.md) \u2014\n  sibling agent-infrastructure services on this host.", "machines/ryzen": "# Hardware\n\n| Part | Value |\n|---|---|\n| CPU | AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D |\n| GPU | Radeon RX 9070 (RDNA4, gfx1201) \u2014 HIP/ROCm target for the engine |\n| RAM | 45 GB |\n| Storage | 3.7 TB NVMe (~299 GB used, 9% \u2014 2026-09-06) |\n| OS | Ubuntu 26.04 LTS \u2014 running kernel 7.0.0-29-generic; `7.0.0-31-generic` installed 2026-09-05 |\n\n> \u26a0\ufe0f **Kernel note (resolved 2026-09-06)**: reboots used to land on the OLD kernel \u2014\n> `/etc/default/grub` was pinned to the `gnulinux-7.0.0-29-generic` entry even\n> though `-31` is installed. agent inference\n  for coding tools routes through the Zyphra proxy; mail flows through the\n  Proton bridge.\n\n# Operations\n\nSee [services](/services/index.md) for the systemd units and docker\ncontainers, [playbooks](/playbooks/index.md) for operational runbooks, and\n[policies](/policies/index.md) for the migration plans and code rules.\n\n# Kernel work\n\n- The GPU/NPU backends are the engine's own kernels \u2014 the HIP stack in\n  [rocm_cpp](/components/rocm-cpp.md) (`librocm_cpp.so`, 47 kernels in\n  `kernels/`), plus the NPU/XDNA DPU path.\n- A hand-written raw-AMDGCN [kernel lab](/components/kernel-lab.md) lives on\n  strixhalo (vecadd + TQ2 ternary GEMV, verified on the real GPU) with a\n  documented set of [gfx1151 findings](/references/amdgcn-gfx1151.md) and the\n  [Netra benchmark methodology](/references/netra-benchmark.md) as the\n  fair-comparison playbook.\n- [Camoufox](/components/camoufox.md), a stealth-browser pi skill, covers\n  Reddit and other pages that block plain HTTP clients.", "playbooks/build-engine": "# Prerequisites\n\n| Package | Version / notes |\n|---|---|\n| OS | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS+ (CachyOS/Arch also works) |\n| Kernel | **6.18.22-lts or 7.x \u2014 not 6.19.x** (issue #1 OPTC hang) |\n| ROCm | **TheRock pip SDK \u2014 PINNED to `10.1.0a20260910`** (device wheel chosen from the DETECTED arch: `gfx1151` on Strix Halo, `gfx1201` on RDNA4). Pin matches the install command below. |\n| CMake | \u2265 3.28 \u00b7 Ninja \u2265 1.12 \u00b7 GCC \u2265 13 (C++20) / \u2265 14 (C++23) |\n\n```bash\nsudo apt update && sudo apt install -y cmake ninja-build build-essential git\n```\n\n# Detect THIS machine's GPU arch. Never assume gfx1151: a gfx1201 box given the\n# gfx1151 device build installs cleanly and then aborts in rocBLAS with an empty\n# Tensile list. The detector fails closed (exit 1) rather than guessing.\nHIP_ARCH=\"$(bash scripts/detect-gfx-targets.sh --cmake)\"          # e.g. gfx1151, or gfx1036;gfx1201\nDEV_PKG=\"$(bash scripts/detect-gfx-targets.sh | sed 's/^/device-/' | paste -sd, -)\"   # e.g. device-gfx1151\necho \"Building for $HIP_ARCH (device packages: $DEV_PKG)\"\n\n# TheRock (pip SDK) \u2014 index and version are PINNED to the matched set verified on gfx1201\n\nInstall into a venv at the documented root (Ubuntu needs `python3-venv`):\n\n```bash\nsudo apt install -y python3-venv libvulkan-dev   # libvulkan-dev: find_package(Vulkan) is required\npython3 -m venv \"$HOME/.cache/pip/therock\"\n\"$HOME/.cache/pip/therock/bin/pip\" install \\\n  --index-url https://nightly.repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-next/ \\\n  \"rocm[libraries,devel,$DEV_PKG]==10.1.0a20260910\"   # arch-derived package + pinned version\n# WHY: `whl-multi-arch` tops out at 10.1.0a20260822, whose base leaves gfx1201\n# cuSPARSE UNSUPPORTED and cuSOLVER INCORRECT (2 of 4 defects live). Only the\n# pinned 10.1.0a20260910 set, on whl-next, closes all four.\n\"$HOME/.cache/pip/therock/bin/rocm-sdk\" init   # expand devel tree + link device wheels (required)\nexport THEROCK_PIP_ROOT=\"$HOME/.cache/pip/therock\"\n```\n\nCMake auto-discovers TheRock: `/opt/rocm-therock` \u2192 `$THEROCK_PIP_ROOT` \u2192\n`~/.cache/lemonade/bin/therock`. **Never** point `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` at\nsystem ROCm (`/opt/rocm`).\n\n**Gotcha (hit 2026-08-25):** the pip SDK's `hip-config.cmake` lives under\n`lib/python3.X/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel/`, but `_find_therock_sdk_base`\nonly scans `~/.local/lib`, `/usr/local/lib`, `/usr/lib`, `/opt/rocm-therock/lib`\n\u2014 not a custom venv. Pass it explicitly or `find_package(hip)` fails:\n\n```bash\nexport THEROCK_SDK_BASE=\"$THEROCK_PIP_ROOT/lib/python3.14/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel\"\nexport CMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=\"$HIP_ARCH\"\n```\n\n# Build\n\n```bash\ncmake -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \\\n  -DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=\"$HIP_ARCH\" \\\n  -DTHEROCK_SDK_BASE=\"$THEROCK_SDK_BASE\"\ncmake --build build --target onebin -j$(nproc)\n```\n\nNotes: NPU/XRT-dependent targets (npu_engine_hybrid, qwen36_moe_probe,\ntest_pipeline_real) are skipped at configure when XRT isn't installed \u2014\nnormal; the embedded Lemonade core + `unified --lemonade` still build and\nserve. Never hardcode `gfx1151`: on a gfx1201 card rocBLAS then aborts with an empty Tensile list. |\n| `cannot find -lamdhip64` | TheRock at `/opt/rocm-therock` or `THEROCK_PIP_ROOT`; never system ROCm |\n| No GPU decode despite build | `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/path/to/zaya/build:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH`; verify model is actually Q4NX |\n| First-inference hang on Strix Halo (issue #1, ~1 in 5 boots) | `export HSA_ENABLE_SDMA=0` \u2014 avoids the OPTC code path |\n| 6.19.x kernel lockup under NPU/GPU load | Use 6.18.22-lts or 7.x; `install.sh` detects and warns |\n\n# Related\n\n- [Run zaya](/playbooks/run-zaya.md) \u2014 weights, run, and API usage.\n- [strixhalo](/machines/strixhalo.md) \u2014 the machine this runs on.", "playbooks/install-lemonade": "# Embedded vs standalone (avoiding redundant work)\n\nOn the [1bit engine](/components/1bit-engine.md) you do **not** install\nLemonade separately \u2014 the engine embeds a vendored fork of the Lemonade\nSDK (`third_party/lemonade`) and runs the server core in-process\n(`unified_server`, `unified_server --lemonade`). Install the standalone\nserver only when you want to run Lemonade on its own (other machines,\nplain local AI).\n\n# Platforms\n\nWindows (MSI), Linux (Ubuntu / Arch / Fedora / Debian), macOS (.pkg from the\nlatest release), and **Docker**. Note: Debian 13 needs the Debian Backports\nrepo for `libcpp-httplib0.41` (Debian 13 ships only 0.18).\n\nFollow the platform instructions at lemonade-server.ai/docs/guide/install.\n\n# Service model\n\nLemonade runs as a lightweight **service** (`lemond`) with three front-ends:\n\n- **GUI** \u2014 desktop app\n- **CLI** \u2014 `lemonade` command; chat in your terminal, configure models\n- **Docker** \u2014 containerized server\n\n# Embeddable Lemonade\n\nA portable build of `lemond` you bundle into your own app (instead of a\nglobal service).
