Pairing status:\n- **Embedded**: the engine's vendored fork is **v11.7.0** (`2b6a7d77`), compiled\n  into `build/1bit` \u2014 no separate Lemonade install needed (built + smoke-tested\n  Aug 2026).\n- **Standalone**: verified pairing 1bit v2026.07+ \u2194 Lemonade **v10.9.0**\n  (and API-stable back to v10.3).\n\n# Related\n\n- [Lemonade Server](/components/lemonade-server.md)\n- [Lemonade API surface](/references/lemonade-api.md)\n- [1bit engine](/components/1bit-engine.md)", "playbooks/max-smoke-test": "# Why\n\nMAX is Modular's serving stack (OpenAI-compatible endpoint, MLIR-compiled\ngraphs, AMD + NVIDIA + CPU). Since Mojo/MAX went open source (Apache 2.0,\nModCon 2026) and Qualcomm owns Modular, it is a candidate reference backend\nfor the [1bit engine](/components/1bit-engine.md) \u2014 as a benchmark yardstick\nand a source of open kernels \u2014 but **not** (yet) a WS-09 router backend:\nits bf16 GPU path is corrupt for modern LLMs on every GPU (see Findings).\n\nThis playbook smoke-tests MAX on an AMD box via Docker: it verifies\n**correctness** (greedy decode of a known model), which is the step that\nspeed-only benchmarks miss.\n\n# Prerequisites\n\n- Docker with AMD GPU access: `/dev/kfd` + `/dev/dri` present on the host\n  (no host ROCm needed \u2014 the image bundles its own).\n- ~25 GB free disk for `modular/max-amd:latest` (~20 GB image).\n- HF Hub access for ungated models (`TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0`,\n  `microsoft/Phi-3.5-mini-instruct`). No `HF_TOKEN` needed for those\n  (unauthenticated downloads just get rate-limited).\n\n# Steps\n\n## 1. Pull and run\n\n```bash\ndocker pull modular/max-amd:latest\n\ndocker run -d --name max-smoke \\\n  --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri \\\n  --group-add video \\\n  --ipc=host \\\n  -p 8000:8000 \\\n  -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \\\n  -v ~/.cache/max_cache:/opt/venv/share/max/.max_cache \\\n  modular/max-amd:latest \\\n  --model microsoft/Phi-3.5-mini-instruct\n```\n\nNotes:\n- `--group-add keep-groups` (shown in current docs) fails on Docker 29.7.2 \u2014\n  use `--group-add video`.\n- With two AMD GPUs present (e.g. RX 9070 `gfx1201` + Granite Ridge iGPU\n  `gfx1036`), MAX enumerates `gpu:0`/`gpu:1` in rocminfo agent order; the\n  default is `gpu[0]`. Pin with `--devices=gpu:0`.\n\n## 2. Wait for ready\n\n```bash\nfor i in $(seq 1 40); do sleep 10\n  curl -s -m 3 http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models >/dev/null && echo \"READY ~$((i*10))s\" && break\ndone\n```\n\nFirst start on a fresh GPU arch compiles the graph (37 s on gfx1201; the\nRDNA2 iGPU took 9+ min for a 3.8B \u2014 compile cost is arch-dependent).\n\n## 3. Correctness check (the important part)\n\n```bash\ncurl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \\\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\\n  -d '{\"model\":\"microsoft/Phi-3.5-mini-instruct\",\n       \"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"What is 2+2? Answer in one short sentence.\"}],\n       \"max_tokens\":64,\"temperature\":0.0}'\n```\n\nGreedy (`temperature: 0`) is the discriminator: sampling artifacts can't\nexplain greedy garbage. **As of MAX 26.5.0 this returns degenerate output**\n(repetition loops, mixed-script token salad) \u2014 see Findings.\n\n## 4. Speed check (numbers are real even when content is not)\n\nStream a completion and measure TTFT + tok/s (or use `max benchmark`\nin-container, which also supports vllm/sglang/trtllm backends for\ncomparison). Reference numbers from the 2026-08-25 run on RX 9070:\nTinyLlama-1.1B ~245 tok/s, TTFT ~17 ms; Phi-3.5-mini ~70 tok/s.\n\n## 5. Cleanup\n\n```bash\ndocker rm -f max-smoke\n```\n\n# Findings (2026-08-25, MAX 26.5.0, `modular/max-amd:latest`)\n\n## Known bug: bf16 GPU path corrupts modern LLM output\n\n- Symptom: `TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0` and `Phi-3.5-mini-instruct` both\n  produce degenerate output (repetition loops, mixed scripts) under greedy\n  **and** sampled decoding. Deterministic across runs; throughput normal.\n- Root cause is upstream and open:\n  - **modular/modular#6883** \u2014 `ops.rms_norm` incorrect when chained after a\n    SwiGLU FFN (bf16 GPU): cosine ~0.40 vs PyTorch; found on H100, so not\n    RDNA-specific.\n  - **modular/modular#6884** \u2014 deterministic numerical corruption compounding\n    across chained transformer blocks (bf16 GPU): forks at block 2, NaN by\n    block 9 with real checkpoints.\n- Both are compilation-level (fusion/scheduling/memory planning), not\n  individual ops \u2014 the same class of backend corruption the engine team\n  fights in aie2p (see [1bit engine](/components/1bit-engine.md) #1769\n  toolchain issues).\n- Repro comments posted on both issues (2026-08-25) from the `max serve`\n  path \u2014 confirming it is reachable without custom Graph API code.\n\n## No dtype workaround on this image\n\n- `--devices=cpu` \u2192 fails: bf16 not compatible with CPU.\n- `--quantization-encoding float16|float8_e4m3fn|q4_k` \u2192 rejected by the\n  MAX engine for HF models; only bf16 (default) is accepted on GPU.\n- So the corrupt bf16 path is the only usable one today.\n\n## What still holds up\n\n- The platform works mechanically: gfx1201 auto-detected, graph compiled,\n  OpenAI API up, real throughput.\n- MAX's kernels and compiler are now open source (Apache 2.0) in\n  `github.com/modular/modular` (`KGEN/` = Mojo compiler, `max/kernels/`,\n  `max/python/max/serve/`) \u2014 worth studying for the engine's GPU path.\n\n# Decision record\n\n| Date | Decision |\n|---|---|\n| 2026-08-25 | Do **not** add MAX to WS-09 / unified_server as an LLM backend until #6883/#6884 are fixed and re-tested. Keep as benchmark reference + kernel source. |\n\n# Re-test checklist (after upstream fix)\n\n1. `max serve` Phi-3.5-mini, greedy \u2014 expect coherent sentence.\n2. Re-run TinyLlama for cross-family confirmation.\n3. Then evaluate strixhalo (gfx1151, 128 GB) with docker installed, for the\n   74B-class serving question.\n\n# Related\n\n- [1bit engine](/components/1bit-engine.md)\n- [Lemonade Server](/components/lemonade-server.md)\n- [Model families](/references/model-families.md)", "playbooks/newsfeed-mirror": "# Newsfeed mirror\n\nThe 1bit.MONSTER guild gets two kinds of inbound content, both driven by one\nscript on ryzen:\n\n| Channel | ID | Content |\n|---|---|---|\n| `#newsfeed` | `1542813807762485248` | Cross-community feeds \u2014 mirrored from other Discord-like servers (Fluxer HQ `#Updates`, `#Platform Status`) |\n| `#announcements` | `1540335289761804288` | Official announcements, incl. **new blog posts** from 1bit.monster |\n\n## Script\n\n`~/fluxer-mcp/scripts/community-feed.mjs` (node, no deps beyond fetch):\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/community-feed.mjs            # incremental (cron every 5 min)\nnode scripts/community-feed.mjs --backfill # post the single most recent item per source\n```\n\n- **Blog job**: fetches `https://1bit.monster/1bit-blog.html`, parses\n  `<article class=\"log-row\">` blocks (date / title / href / summary), and\n  posts new posts to `#announcements` via the **Blog Publisher** webhook\n  (username `1bit.MONSTER Blog`).\n- **HQ job**: polls Fluxer HQ `#Updates` (`1458584080423879232`) and\n  `#Platform Status` (`1486764961039533570`) after a stored cursor and posts\n  new messages to `#newsfeed` via the **Newsfeed Ingest** webhook, with the\n  username set to `<author> \u00b7 <source label>`, rich embeds preserved,\n  `@everyone`/`@here` neutralized.\n- **First-run seeding**: with no state file the script seeds cursors/seen\n  posts from current content and posts nothing \u2014 the channel never floods.\n\n## State & credentials (all under `~/fluxer-mcp/state/`)\n\n| File | Contents | Perms |\n|---|---|---|\n| `feed-state.json` | per-source message cursors + seen blog post URLs | 600 |\n| `webhooks.json` | Newsfeed Ingest + Blog Publisher webhook id/token | 600 |\n| `feed.log` | run log (also mirrored to `~/.local/share/community-feed.log` via cron) | 644 |\n\n## Scheduling\n\nCron (ryzen \u2014 source of truth for ~/fluxer-mcp; strixhalo mirrors it with --delete):\n\n```\n*/5 * * * * cd /home/bcloud/fluxer-mcp && /home/bcloud/.nvm/versions/node/v24.19.0/bin/node scripts/community-feed.mjs >> /home/bcloud/.local/share/community-feed.log 2>&1\n```\n\nEdits to `~/fluxer-mcp` must be made on **ryzen** \u2014 strixhalo's copy is wiped by\n`sync-agent-setup.sh` every 5 min.\n\n## Instatus flood guard (`newsfeed-instatus-guard.py`)\n\nFluxer platform incidents make the Instatus status webhook replay full digests\n(one message per component/region) into the source channel. The mirror passes\nthem through 1:1, so a guard collapses them: it keeps only the NEWEST Instatus\nmessage in each newsfeed and deletes the rest.\n\n- Location: `~/.local/bin/newsfeed-instatus-guard.py` (runs on **strixhalo** only)\n- Cron: `*/5 * * * * /usr/bin/python3 ~/.local/bin/newsfeed-instatus-guard.py >> ~/.local/share/newsfeed-guard.log 2>&1`\n- Targets: Discord #newsfeed + Fluxer #newsfeed (auth via `state/discord-bot.json` / `.env`)\n- Idempotent: prints `no instatus spam` when there is nothing to clean.\n\nGotchas that bit us (2026-09-03):\n- Discord needs `Authorization: Bot <token>` (raw token \u2192 silent 401 no-op).\n- Filter on the Instatus **username/embed** (`Instatus` in the mirror username\n  or a `fluxerstatus.com` embed), NOT the webhook id \u2014 both feed sources\n  (`#Updates` and `#Platform Status`) are mirrored through the same webhook.\n\n## Adding a feed source\n\n1. Add an entry to `SOURCES` in the script: `{ key, channel, label }` \u2014 the\n   bot must be able to read that channel (member + VIEW_CHANNEL).\n2. Optionally delete `state/feed-state.json` cursors for that key (or run\n   `--backfill` to post the latest item immediately).\n3. Cursor semantics: `GET /channels/{id}/messages?after={cursor}` returns\n   oldest-first; the cursor advances per successfully posted message.\n\n## External pushes (webhooks)\n\nThe webhooks are not just used by the mirror \u2014 they are the ingest point for\nany external source (RSS bridge, CI, other communities). Executing:\n\n```\nPOST {FLUXER_API_BASE_URL}/webhooks/{webhook_id}/{token}?wait=true\nBody: { content?, username?, avatar_url?, embeds? }\n```\n\n`FLUXER_API_BASE_URL` is `https://api.fluxer.app/v1` (see\n`~/fluxer-mcp/.env`).\n\n## Gotchas\n\n- **Fluxer's messages API returns `?after=` results NEWEST-first** (Discord\n  returns oldest-first). `community-feed.mjs` sorts by id before posting so the\n  cursor lands on the NEWEST message of each batch \u2014 without that, the cursor\n  sticks at the OLDEST and every 5-min run re-posts the same batch (the\n  2026-09-03 Instatus flood: ~100 msgs re-posted per run per channel).\n- Webhook execute replies `204`/empty unless `?wait=true` is set \u2014 always\n  pass it and tolerate an empty body.\n- Source messages may contain `@everyone` \u2014 always neutralize before\n  re-posting into a different guild.\n- 4000-char content cap per message; long posts are truncated at 3900.\n- Custom emoji (`<:name:id>`) from the source guild won't render in\n  1bit.MONSTER \u2014 they degrade to raw text, which is acceptable.", "playbooks/pr-agent-workflow": "# Flow\n\n1. A PR lands in [1bit-MONSTER/1bit-MONSTER](https://github.com/1bit-MONSTER/1bit-MONSTER).\n2. The self-hosted runner\n   (`actions.runner.1bit-MONSTER.1bit-MONSTER.ryzen-pr-agent`) on\n   [ryzen](/machines/ryzen.md) picks up the workflow.\n3. The PR agent reviews / gates the change per the\n   [code-intelligence policy](/policies/code-intelligence.md):\n   impact analysis before edits, `detect_changes()` before commits, warning\n   on HIGH/CRITICAL risk.\n\n# Agent responsibilities (from AGENTS.md)\n\n- Impact analysis on every edited symbol, blast radius reported.\n- `detect_changes()` before committing; compare against `main` for regressions.\n- Never find-and-replace renames; never commit without change detection.\n\n# Related\n\n- [Code intelligence policy](/policies/code-intelligence.md)\n- [1bit engine](/components/1bit-engine.md)", "playbooks/refresh-knowledge": "# Manual refresh\n\n```bash\n~/okf/scripts/refresh.sh           # validate + snapshot + drift check + viz\n~/okf/scripts/refresh.sh --commit  # same, plus git commit if anything changed\n```\n\nWhat it does:\n\n1. **Validate** \u2014 runs `okf-validate` over the bundle (conformance, 0 errors expected).\n2. **Snapshot** \u2014 captures live facts: listening ports (+ owning process), the\n   platform's systemd services, and docker containers; writes\n   `~/.cache/okf/current.json`.\n3. **Drift** \u2014 diffs against the previous snapshot; prints added/removed\n   services, containers, and ports. Drift means the bundle is out of date.\n4. **Viz** \u2014 regenerates `viz.html` with the [reference-agent visualizer](/playbooks/restart-service.md).\n5. **Site** \u2014 regenerates the static docs website (`site/`) with `scripts/site.py` (one HTML page per concept, nav, search, backlinks).\n6. **Fingerprint** \u2014 `scripts/check-generated.sh --write` records `{source .md \u2192 sha256}` in\n   `GENERATED.json` and re-reads it, so the run that generates the tree also files and verifies\n   the evidence that the tree matches the prose. Run `scripts/check-generated.sh` (no argument)\n   after any prose edit: it exits 1 naming the changed file, which is how a prose commit that\n   forgot to regenerate is caught instead of shipping stale pages (Rule 12).\n\n# Machine-dependence of the generated tree\n\nThe generated output used to carry the **absolute bundle root** in every page footer, so the\nsame prose generated on ryzen and on strixhalo produced 88 differing pages with no content\nchange, and a copy generated at another root never matched. `scripts/site.py` now emits the\nOKF-root-relative label (`systems/1bit-monster`), which removes that channel entirely.\n\nTwo host-derived strings remain, and they are **not** interchangeable with the one above:\n\n- **External `resource:` values** in frontmatter (`file:///home/bcloud/projects/1bit-MONSTER/\u2026`,\n  `~/iron/\u2026`, `~/npu-ab/\u2026`) are rendered into their own site pages and into `viz.html`, so those\n  four pages and the visualiser still differ per machine. A host-free form is possible \u2014 the\n  bundle already uses `resource: strixhalo:192.168.50.110` in two concepts \u2014 but choosing it is a\n  convention decision, not a bug fix, and it touches docs owned by more than one agent.\n- **Paths quoted in prose** (28 site pages, 92 strings in `viz.html`) are *content*: they are\n  identical on both mirrors because the markdown is synced, so they cause no churn. A doc that\n  quotes a command is legitimately host-specific and generation cannot remove it.\n\nSo: idempotence holds **per bundle root** (regenerating at a different root is a different test),\nand after the footer fix the only per-machine churn left is the four external resources plus\n`viz.html`.\n\n# History sync between the two mirrors\n\n**Content converges on a schedule, in both directions.** `scripts/rsync-sync.sh` runs every ten\nminutes on *both* machines, staggered five minutes apart (ryzen `5,15,25,35,45,55`; strixhalo\n`0,10,20,30,40,50`) \u2014 exactly as the script's header describes \u2014 and since `63b20b71` it excludes\n`.git`, which matches the stated design: each machine keeps its own local history.\n\n**`.git` does not cross on that schedule \u2014 measured in both directions, each with a positive\ncontrol.** A probe object placed on one host stayed absent on the other in both runs, while a\nfilesystem marker placed the same way crossed in both \u2014 so \"absent\" means the sync ran and did not\ncarry the object, rather than that it did nothing. The exclusion is effective as cron runs it, and\nthe dry run agrees (20 `.git` entries offered without the flag, 0 with it).\n\n**The identical histories that prompted this section came from outside the schedule.** Both clones\nsat at `ae6cdcd12` with `.git/logs/HEAD` byte-identical (`sha256 88b2c4aa\u2026`) \u2014 a file only local git\noperations write, so it cannot arrive by fetch or bundle, and `/tmp/okf.bundle` carries only\n`5101597d\u2026`, neither of the two commits. The route was therefore an ad-hoc transfer or a window in\nwhich the sending host still ran the pre-exclusion script. Which of the two is **not established**,\nand is not asserted here.\n\n**There was a second route, and it was the one that moved `.git` \u2014 closed 2026-09-11.** strixhalo\nran `sync-agent-setup.sh` every five minutes, and its line 38 pulled the whole directory from ryzen:\n`rsync -azu -e ssh bcloud@ryzen:/home/bcloud/okf/ /home/bcloud/okf/`, with no `--exclude=.git`. The\nexclusion in `rsync-sync.sh` was real but that script was not the only sync of this directory, so\ncommits made on ryzen reached the mirror within five minutes while commits made on strixhalo had no\nroute back.\n\n**Dated note \u2014 applied 2026-09-11T18:36Z (option 1).** Line 38 now reads\n`rsync -azu --exclude=.git -e \u2026 /home/bcloud/okf/`; nothing else in the script changed \u2014 `diff`\nagainst the backup is that one line, `bash -n` is clean, the deliberate `MIRROR_ARGS` mirrors are\nuntouched, and the cron still points at it. Controlled both ways on strixhalo: a dry run of the line\noffered **124** `.git` entries without the flag and **0** with it, and a probe object written on ryzen\nstayed absent after a live run. So **no scheduled route moves history in either direction** from that\nmoment on; the paragraphs above describe the pre-fix behaviour this note supersedes, kept as history\nrather than rewritten.\n\nCurrent consequences:\n\n- **no scheduled route moves a commit in either direction** \u2014 the manual recipe in\n  [machines/strixhalo.md](/machines/strixhalo.md) is the only route, so both clones drift apart until\n  someone runs it;\n- refs quoted in the bundle (`SOURCE_REV`, commit ids in `log.md`) still need the comparison \u2014\n  `git rev-parse HEAD` on both clones \u2014 because they agree only just after the recipe has been run;\n- a commit on either clone is stranded until then, and until the script is adopted into the repo the\n  **fix itself** is a dotfile that a rebuild would lose (see the open item below).\n\n**The mirror's working tree is permanently dirty, by design.** Files converge while its index and HEAD\nstay frozen \u2014 measured on strixhalo: **8 `git status --porcelain` lines** (seven modified, the adopted\nscript untracked) with HEAD at `412df24c`, i.e. the mirror's tip while ryzen was at `70334ce9e`\n(2026-09-11T19:15Z). Note the two kinds of number in that sentence, because they behave differently:\n**the `8` status lines are stable** (they are a set of changed files, reproduced independently by a\nsecond reader), while **the lag is a claim about a moment** \u2014 it was 3 when this paragraph was first\nwritten, 5 when a peer read it twenty minutes later, and 6 when the pair above was measured, because\nevery commit on ryzen moves it. Quote the **pair of revs and the moment**, never the count.\n\nTheir horizons differ, and precisely: **the count moves on the next commit anywhere, while the set-number moves\nonly when the set's *membership* changes** \u2014 a file entering or leaving it, not an already-dirty file being edited\nagain. Measured across four observations by two agents: the count walked **3 \u2192 5 \u2192 6 \u2192 7 \u2192 8** while the set stayed\nat `8` lines throughout, including two commits that re-edited files already in it. So the set is quotable for\nlonger, not forever \u2014 the durable form for both remains a ref or a content hash, and the set is merely the cheaper\nof the two to keep honest.\n\n**And the freeze is the mechanism behind both horizons**, which is why they differ at all: the mirror's HEAD cannot\nmove, so membership can only change through a **content event on ryzen** \u2014 a new file reaching the tree, a\ndeletion, or a set-file restored to match the frozen HEAD \u2014 never through a commit. The set's horizon is therefore\n*until the next membership event* and the count's is *until the next commit*: one measures drift against a fixed\nreference, the other distance from it. Verified across five commits and five observations by two agents \u2014 every\ncommit's file list sat entirely inside the set (**12/12** paths \"in set: YES\"), so the count moved five times while\nmembership moved zero.\n\nTwo consequences for anyone working there: **a clean tree is not a signal on the mirror**, and it will\nnever be clean again while the pull excludes `.git`; and **do not \"fix\" it by committing** \u2014 a commit\nthere has no route back and would duplicate content that already exists on ryzen as different commits,\nwhich is the stranded-commit hazard above in its most likely form. When a freshness signal is genuinely\nneeded, use `git rev-parse HEAD` against ryzen's or a content hash against the source, not the\nworking-tree status.\n\n**Open items for the owner:**\n\n1. ~~**Add `--exclude=.git` to `sync-agent-setup.sh:38`**~~ \u2014 **done, 2026-09-11T18:36Z**, see the dated\n   note above. Applied on strixhalo by the peer after the owner chose this option, and verified\n   independently here by reading the line, the `diff` against the backup (that line only), `bash -n`,\n   and re-running the dry-run control both ways \u2014 **124** `.git` entries offered without the flag and\n   **0** with it \u2014 with a fresh probe object staying absent after a live run.\n2. **Adopt the script into the repo \u2014 DONE 2026-09-11** (the commit that added\n   `scripts/sync-agent-setup.sh`). The file is the live dotfile's content **verbatim** (source sha256\n   `06568096b80954336cab936923922c13`, which included the `--exclude=.git` fix) with a header added\n   saying what it pulls, why the exclusion matters, and that it is executed **by path** \u2014 so it is\n   committed mode `100755`, because a 644 script invoked by path fails with exit 126 and reads as\n   *the check failed* rather than *the check never ran*. Precedent for hosting a machine script here:\n   `scripts/{rsync-sync.sh,refresh.sh,site.py,rocm-hub-digest.py}`.\n\n   **Deliberate divergence:** the dotfile at `~/.local/bin/sync-agent-setup.sh` stays in place,\n   frozen, as the revert path; cron now points at the repo copy. So the two differ by that header\n   and will not track each other \u2014 stated here and in the file's own header rather than left to be\n   rediscovered. Note what adoption does and does not buy: the **content** is now versioned and\n   reviewable, while the cron line and its target path remain machine-local provisioning that a\n   rebuild still has to restore \u2014 which is why the requirement lives in this playbook.\n\n   Host-side half (the cycle that proves it): repoint the crontab line, `bash -n` it, confirm the\n   crontab, then watch one full `*/5` run and verify three things \u2014 the cron ran (fresh log line), the\n   pull still works (a file created on ryzen arrives), and the okf line **still excludes `.git`** (a\n   ryzen-only probe object stays absent). The third is the one that matters: the change is meant to be\n   invisible to what the script excludes.\n\n   Superseded and kept as history: a scheduled fast-forward-only strixhalo \u2192 ryzen route, or leaving\n   the pull as the deliberate history route \u2014 the latter kept the file-level `.git` copy hazard, which\n   is now removed. The throwaway-commit experiment that would have tested it is moot for the same reason: with\nno route moving history in either direction, a strixhalo-local commit is stranded by construction.\n\n# When drift is reported\n\nThe [port map](/references/ports.md), [services](/services/index.md), and the\ncomponent docs are the sources of truth. Update the affected concept(s):\n\n1. Edit the concept doc (e.g. a new port \u2192 `references/ports.md`).\n2. Bump `generated.at` to the refresh time (actor `pi/coding-agent`).\n3. Optionally add a `log.md` entry.\n4. Commit \u2014 `git -C ~/okf add -A && git -C ~/okf commit`.\n\n# Automated refresh\n\nA systemd user timer runs the refresh daily:\n\n```bash\nsystemctl --user status okf-refresh.timer      # next run time\nsystemctl --user list-timers | grep okf        # schedule\njournalctl --user -u okf-refresh.service       # last run output\n```\n\nThe timer only validates/snapshots/regenerates \u2014 it never commits, so an\nagent or human reviews drift before anything is written to git.", "playbooks/restart-service": "# System services\n\n```bash\nsudo systemctl restart open-design.service      # OpenDesign daemon (port 7456)\nsudo systemctl status  actions.runner.1bit-MONSTER.ryzen-pr-agent.service\n```\n\n# User services\n\n```bash\nsystemctl --user restart zyphra-proxy.service\nsystemctl --user list-timers                     # zyphra-balance-monitor.timer\n```\n\n# Docker (Root bot / Root MCP)\n\n```bash\ndocker ps                                       # find container (node:24-slim)\ndocker logs --tail 50 <container>               # diagnose\ndocker restart <container>\n```\n\n# Diagnose a port\n\n```bash\nss -tlnp | grep :<port>        # who owns the port (see [port map](/references/ports.md))\n```\n\n# Related\n\n- [Services & ports](/services/index.md)", "playbooks/run-zaya": "# Weights\n\nZaya1-8B weights are flat float16 `.bin` files under `/tmp/zaya_weights/`,\none file per tensor named after the HF-style key (e.g.\n`model_embed_tokens_weight.bin`, `model_layers_0_self_attn_o_proj_weight.bin`,\n\u00d7 40 layers). ~6 GB fp16 + MoE params in GPU memory. Download from the\nreleases page or export from an HF checkpoint.\n\n# Run\n\n```bash\nsource env.sh          # sets HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.5.1 etc.\n./build/1bit zaya                    # default port 8088\n./build/1bit zaya --port 8080        # custom port\n./build/1bit zaya --model /path/to/model.h1b\n```\n\n# Health + generate\n\n```bash\ncurl http://localhost:8088/                                    # {\"status\":\"ok\",\"model\":\"Zaya1-8B\",...}\ncurl -X POST http://localhost:8088/completion -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\\n  -d '{\"prompt\":\"The future of AI is\",\"n_predict\":32}'\n# \u2192 {\"tokens\":[...],\"text\":\"...\",\"gen_ms\":2850.12,\"tok_s\":11.2}\n```\n\nOpenAI-compatible: `POST /v1/chat/completions`, `POST /v1/batch/completions`,\n`GET /v1/models`, plus A2A agent-card endpoints. See the\n[zaya server API](/references/zaya-server-api.md).\n\n# Performance (Strix Halo, Radeon 8060S)\n\n| Configuration | tok/s |\n|---|---|\n| Prefill (32 tok) | ~18 |\n| Decode (32 tok) | ~11 |\n| Decode (64 tok) | ~10 |\n\nDecode speed is bound by GPU memory bandwidth; MoE expert memory pressure\n(16 experts \u00d7 2 layers) matters.\n\n# Troubleshooting\n\n| Symptom | Fix |\n|---|---|\n| `amdclang++: command not found` | `export PATH=/opt/rocm/bin:/opt/rocm/lib/llvm/bin:$PATH` |\n| `hipErrorNoBinaryForGpu` | `source env.sh` (`HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.5.1`) |\n| Missing weights | Extract to `/tmp/zaya_weights/` |\n| `hipMalloc failed` | Need ~6 GB free GPU memory; check `rocm-smi` |\n| `bind: Address already in use` | `--port <other>` |\n\n# Related\n\n- [Build the engine](/playbooks/build-engine.md)\n- [zaya server API](/references/zaya-server-api.md)\n- [1bit engine](/components/1bit-engine.md)", "playbooks/support-tickets": "# Support tickets\n\nOfficial support works on two tracks \u2014 **file an issue** (GitHub, tracked) or\n**ask in chat** (ticket per request). Solved tickets are archived so future\nmembers find the answer.\n\n## Channels\n\n| Channel | ID | Read-only | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `#support` | `1541773739480317952` | no | entry point (site footer invite lands here); pinned \"how to get help\" |\n| `#issue-tracker` | `1542815632767062016` | yes | live mirror of `1bit-MONSTER/1bit-MONSTER` issues |\n| `#support-archive` | `1542815449803141120` | yes | resolved tickets, for future reference |\n| `Support Tickets` category | `1542815414138974208` | \u2014 | one channel per open request (the \"thread\") |\n\nTopics on `#general` and `#support` point people at the GitHub issue tracker\nfirst: `https://github.com/1bit-MONSTER/1bit-MONSTER/issues`.\n\n## Workflow\n\n1. **User asks for help** in `#support` or `#general`.\n2. **Open a ticket** (creates a dedicated channel + copies the request):\n\n   ```bash\n   node scripts/open-ticket.mjs <channel_id> <message_id> [title]   # dry-run\n   node scripts/open-ticket.mjs <channel_id> <message_id> [title] --apply\n   ```\n\n   Creates `#ticket-<n>-<slug>` under Support Tickets, posts the request\n   (content + embeds), and records the source message id.\n3. **Solve it** in the ticket channel (engineers/mods answer there).\n4. **Archive + close** (copies full transcript to #support-archive, then\n   deletes the ticket channel):\n\n   ```bash\n   node scripts/solve-ticket.mjs <ticket_channel_id>          # dry-run\n   node scripts/solve-ticket.mjs <ticket_channel_id> --apply\n   ```\n\nBoth scripts dry-run by default; `--apply` executes. Fluxer has no native\nthreads (channel types 11/5/6 rejected by the API), so \"thread\" = one channel\nper request.\n\n## Issue tracker mirror\n\n`scripts/github-issues.mjs` polls `gh api` (authenticated as\n`bong-water-water-bong` on ryzen) and posts to `#issue-tracker` via the\n**GitHub Issues** webhook:\n\n- \ud83c\udd95 new issue (green embed), \u2705 closed (purple), \ud83d\udd04 reopened (amber)\n- fetches all open issues + 30 recently-updated closed issues, filters PRs\n- first run seeds state without posting; state in `state/github-issues.json`\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/github-issues.mjs             # incremental (cron)\nnode scripts/github-issues.mjs --backfill  # post most recently updated issue\n```\n\n## Scheduling (ryzen \u2014 source of truth)\n\n```\n*/5 * * * * cd /home/bcloud/fluxer-mcp && node scripts/community-feed.mjs  >> ~/.local/share/community-feed.log 2>&1\n*/5 * * * * cd /home/bcloud/fluxer-mcp && node scripts/github-issues.mjs   >> ~/.local/share/github-issues.log 2>&1\n```\n\nWebhook tokens for `#newsfeed` / `#announcements` / `#issue-tracker` live in\n`~/fluxer-mcp/state/webhooks.json` (600).\n\n## Gotchas\n\n- **~/fluxer-mcp on strixhalo is a mirror**: `sync-agent-setup.sh` rsyncs\n  ryzen \u2192 strixhalo with `--delete` every 5 min. Any new script/state must be\n  pushed to ryzen (`rsync -a file bcloud@192.168.50.100:~/fluxer-mcp/...`) or\n  it is wiped on strixhalo. Run the crons on ryzen only.\n- Read-only channels are enforced with an @everyone `deny: 2048`\n  (SEND_MESSAGES) overwrite \u2014 the `fluxer_*` tools don't expose overwrites, so\n  create them via the raw API (see `fluxer-mcp/scripts` for examples).\n- Ticket transcripts are capped at 4000 chars when archived; long tickets are\n  truncated.", "playbooks/sync-lemonade-fork": "# When\n\nUpstream `lemonade-sdk/lemonade` has moved and the fork (or the local `main`)\nis behind. Context and people: [Lemonade upstream contribution](/references/lemonade-upstream-contribution.md).\n\n# Procedure\n\n```bash\ncd ~/projects/\"lemonade sdk\"/lemonade\ngit fetch --all --prune\ngit rev-list --left-right --count main...origin/main     # expect 0 <N>\n\n# 1. upstream line: fast-forward only\ngit merge --ff-only origin/main\n\n# 2. fork default branch: merge, don't rebase (it is published and already has merges)\ngit worktree add -b fork-main ~/wt/fork-main-sync fork/main   # if not present\ncd ~/wt/fork-main-sync\ngit merge --no-commit --no-ff origin/main\n# ... resolve conflicts (rules below) ...\ngit commit && git push fork fork-main:main\n```\n\n# Conflict-resolution rules\n\nThe fork's delta is small and known; upstream's 90+ commits are not. Resolve in\nupstream's favour wherever the fork merely duplicated a fix.\n\n| File | Rule |\n|------|------|\n| `.github/workflows/validate_llamacpp.yml` | take **upstream** \u2014 upstream landed its own `b[NUM]` tag resolution, so the fork's copy is a duplicate |\n| `src/cpp/resources/defaults.json`, `docs/guide/configuration/README.md` | take **upstream** (they are generated), then confirm the fork's `mlx-engine` block survived the auto-merge |\n| `README.md` | union; **recompute the `Text generation` `rowspan`** (it was 14 after adding `llamacpp-hrx`, `ds4` and the 3 `mlx-engine` rows) |\n| `docs/dev/backends-reference.md` | union. The auto-merge interleaves the `llamacpp-hrx` and `mlx-engine` sections \u2014 split them back into two headed sections, each with its own `ctx_size` row |\n| `docs/guide/configuration/custom-models.md` | union the generated `recipe-values` list (upstream's new recipes **plus** `mlx-engine`) |\n| `src/cpp/resources/server_models.json` | union the model blocks \u2014 **add the missing comma** between them, then parse-check |\n\n# Verification before pushing\n\n```bash\ngit grep -n '^<<<<<<< \\|^>>>>>>> ' -- .                 # no markers\npython3 -c \"import json;json.load(open('src/cpp/resources/server_models.json'))\"\npython3 -c \"import json;json.load(open('src/cpp/resources/defaults.json'))\"\ngit diff --stat origin/main                              # only the fork's own intent\ncmake -S . -B /tmp/lemonade-cfg -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release   # ~20 s; runs descriptor codegen\ngrep -c mlx /tmp/lemonade-cfg/include/backend_descriptors_generated.h\n```\n\n`git diff --stat origin/main` is the strongest single check: after a correct\nmerge it lists **only** the fork's intended files (mlx sources + descriptor,\n`CMakeLists.txt`, generated docs/version artifacts, `mlx-engine` config and\nmodels, and the `.github/workflows/build-container.yml` ghcr-org fix).\n\n# Traps\n\n- A fork PR branch may have been **force-pushed by a maintainer** (a rebase onto\n  the new upstream tip). Compare patch-ids before resetting a PR worktree:\n  `git show <sha> | git patch-id --stable`. Only `git reset --hard fork/<branch>`\n  when the patch-ids match.\n- Downstream files that upstream has since **tracked** block a fast-forward as\n  \"untracked working tree files would be overwritten\" (16 such paths on\n  ryzen, 2026-09-15). Diff each against `origin/main` first; if identical (or a\n  subset), move them aside and delete \u2014 a backup went to\n  `~/tmp/lemonade-untracked-backup-<timestamp>`.\n- Never post a PR comment about the sync: Rule 1 of the upstream\n  [AI content policy](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/lemonade/blob/main/docs/dev/ai-content-policy.md)\n  bans AI prose in PRs, issues and discussions. Report to the human.\n\n# Related\n\n- [Lemonade upstream contribution](/references/lemonade-upstream-contribution.md)\n- [Install Lemonade](install-lemonade.md)", "policies/code-intelligence": "# Always Do\n\n- **Run impact analysis before editing any symbol** \u2014 `impact({target, direction: \"upstream\"})` and report the blast radius (callers, processes, risk level).\n- **Run `detect_changes()` before committing** \u2014 verify only expected symbols/flows changed; compare against `main` for regression review.\n- **Warn on HIGH/CRITICAL impact risk** before proceeding with edits.\n- Explore unfamiliar code with `query()` (execution flows) instead of grepping; use `context()` for full symbol context.\n- For security review, use `explain()` (taint findings; needs `analyze --pdg`).\n\n# Never Do\n\n- NEVER edit a function/class/method without first running `impact` on it.\n- NEVER ignore HIGH or CRITICAL impact warnings.\n- NEVER rename symbols with find-and-replace \u2014 use `rename` (call-graph aware).\n- NEVER commit without `detect_changes()`.\n\n# Index\n\n- GitNexus index: `gitnexus://repo/1bit-MONSTER/context` (freshness check),\n  `.../clusters`, `.../processes`.\n- Stale index? `node .gitnexus/run.cjs analyze` from the repo root.", "policies/lemonade-local-only": "# lemonade-sdk stays local\n\nThe lemonade-sdk maintainers reacted negatively to agent activity on\n`lemonade-sdk/lemonade` (issue-triage comments, close requests, and a\nsubmitted fix PR \u2014 #3425 \u2014 that was closed after \"changes requested\").\nWe thought we were helping; the maintainers read it as noise from an agent\nthat didn't understand their documentation. Lesson recorded: **stay local**.\n\n## Rule\n\n**No \"calling home\" to lemonade-sdk/lemonade.** Concretely, without explicit\nper-user approval, do NOT:\n\n- close / reopen / label / comment on issues\n- open, push, or comment on PRs\n- request reviews or mention/ping maintainers (`@fl0rianr`, `@jeremyfowers`, \u2026)\n- reply to or act on lemonade GitHub notification emails\n\nAllowed (read-only, for context):\n\n- `gh issue view` / `gh api GET` on lemonade-sdk/lemonade\n- reading emails that report lemonade activity (report to the user, do not act)\n- working on the **local checkout** at `~/projects/lemonade sdk/lemonade`:\n  read code, build, test, draft patches \u2014 but do not push or submit anything\n\nIf the user asks to interact with the remote repo again, warn them about this\npolicy first and get explicit confirmation.\n\n## Why\n\n- The account `bong-water-water-bong` has only triage-level permission anyway\n  (can comment, cannot close) \u2014 remote write actions are half-broken by design.\n- The maintainers' process expects their own triage bot + maintainer closes;\n  external comments read as noise.\n- Our value is local: analysis, fixes, and understanding \u2014 not GitHub chatter.\n\n## Related\n\n- Local checkout: `~/projects/lemonade sdk/lemonade` (fork, branch `main`)\n- Credential reality: see `credential-vault` skill (`~/Documents/github pat \u2026`)\n\n## SCOPE NOTE (added 2026-09-10)\n\nThis policy is about **contact with the upstream GitHub repo** \u2014 it is **not** a ban on\nediting the vendored tree. `third_party/lemonade` in the engine repo **is** the\nauthoritative local-only source, and local deltas are the normal way change lands there\n(35 commits had touched it by 2026-09-10, including `fix(lemonade):` ones).\n\nConfusion is easy and has happened: an agent carried \"do not touch `third_party/lemonade`\"\nas a constraint on the strength of *this* policy. That is an over-read. Editing the\nvendored tree is allowed; **posting anything to `lemonade-sdk/lemonade` is not.**\n\nWhat the vendored tree *does* require is provenance care, and that is documented in the\ntree itself (`third_party/lemonade/UPSTREAM.md`): it is **refreshed FROM**\n`/home/bcloud/1bit-lemonade-v1170/third_party/lemonade`, so a local delta that exists only\nin the engine copy is **deleted by the next refresh** unless it is also landed in v1170 and\nlisted in `UPSTREAM.md`'s local-delta list.", "policies/migration-omarchy": "> \u26d4 **ABANDONED 2026-08-27** \u2014 this migration was a dream, not a plan.\n> Decision: **ryzen stays on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS**; no OS cut-over. The checklist\n> below is kept only as a record (the ROCm/RDNA4 risk note and the root-bot\n> git-hygiene action remain valid independently of any migration).\n\n# Scope\n\nTarget machine: **ryzen** (AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D + Radeon RX 9070 RDNA4, 45 GB\nRAM, 3.7 TB NVMe), currently Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. Peer machine\n[strixhalo](/machines/strixhalo.md) stays as-is.\n\n# First-class risk\n\n**ROCm/HIP support for the RX 9070 (gfx1201 / RDNA4)** \u2014 the\n[1bit engine](/components/1bit-engine.md) pins `ROCm/FastFlowLM` as a\nsubmodule, so the GPU target is HIP/ROCm-based. ROCm on RDNA4 is newer/less\nmature. Distro-independent: test the GPU path on Ubuntu first, or explicitly\naccept CPU-only for now. Arch gives a *newer* ROCm (more likely to work),\nbut don't migrate on that assumption.\n\n# Phase 0 \u2014 git hygiene (do first)\n\n- [ ] `~/1bit-monster/root-bot` has **no git repo** \u2014 `git init`, commit,\n      push to GitHub *before* touching the disk. Its `.env` holds a secret\n      token: ensure it's `.gitignore`d and never committed.\n- [ ] Push all dirty state in every repo (engine, fluxer-mcp, \u2026).\n\n# Status\n\nActive plan; phases beyond Phase 0 follow the checklist in the source doc.", "policies/multi-agent-graph-orchestration": "# Always do\n\n- **Match the structure to the problem.** Independent signals (logs / metrics /\n  traces; or per-file audits, per-repo checks, per-candidate reviews) \u2192 a graph:\n  one specialist per signal in parallel, a coordinator that correlates.\n  Sequential reasoning that must share state \u2192 a loop. Do not fan out work that\n  is genuinely serial, and do not serialize work that is genuinely parallel.\n- **One signal per specialist.** Each node reads exactly one input and ignores\n  the rest. State this in its task text, including what to ignore. A node that\n  can read everything is not a specialist.\n- **The briefing is the edge.** A node's scope lives in its task/briefing text,\n  not in code. Re-scoping the graph = rewriting the briefings.\n- **The coordinator analyzes nothing itself.** It fans out, waits, then\n  correlates the specialists' artifacts into: root cause \u2192 evidence (one line per\n  signal) \u2192 confidence \u2192 remediation \u2192 **other suspects considered and why\n  rejected**.\n- **Fan out all nodes, then wait once.** Launch every lane in the same step and\n  take the result at the dependency barrier. No interleaved spawn-wait-spawn.\n- **Bind durable output.** Each node writes a fixed artifact path (the\n  `findings.md` role): declare it as the run's output binding, never rely on task\n  prose or a transcript to carry the result forward.\n- **Bounded retry: exactly one.** If the signals do not converge, re-run the\n  nodes **once** with the other nodes' findings attached to each task, then\n  terminate and report the disagreement \u2014 never loop until agreement.\n- **Topology by configuration, not trust.** The coordinator may reach only the\n  agents on an explicit allowlist (who exists/who may be spawned). Enumerate the\n  reachable agents up front; anything off-list is unreachable by design.\n- **One writer per workspace.** Isolate concurrent writers (worktree / separate\n  cwd, or disjoint paths); claim shared paths before editing them.\n\n# Never do\n\n- Never let a specialist see another signal \"for context\" \u2014 that silently\n  converts the graph into one general-purpose agent with extra steps.\n- Never let the coordinator do the correlation work of a node, or a node\n  summarize the whole graph.\n- Never pre-clean or create a specialist's findings file on its behalf; the\n  producer owns its artifact.\n- Never exceed one retry cycle to force agreement.\n- Never report a multi-signal conclusion without naming the suspects the\n  correlation **rejected** \u2014 the noisy-but-healthy signal is the whole point.\n- Never accept a corroborated-sounding claim from one signal when the other\n  signals are neutral: that is the noise trap (see the reference page).\n\n# Mapping onto our primitives\n\n| Graph element (tutorial) | Here |\n| --- | --- |\n| Node (`openclaw agents add`, own workspace) | Specialist subagent run with `context:\"fresh\"` (isolated state), or an external CLI agent; per-node cwd/worktree |\n| Typed edge (`AGENTS.md` briefing) | The run's `task` text \u2014 one input artifact named, the rest explicitly out of scope |\n| Fan-out (`sessions_spawn` \u00d7 N) | Launch every lane in one workflow call |\n| Fan-in (`sessions_yield`) | Await the lanes (`runs.all` / dependency barrier); coordinator correlates |\n| Adjacency list (`allowAgents`) | The explicit agent/persona set the coordinator is permitted to spawn |\n| Bounded cycle (one-retry rule) | One re-run pass with peers' findings appended, then finish |\n| `findings.md` | The run's bound output artifact (path declared, not implied) |\n| Gateway restart after edits | Re-load briefings/skills after changing them; stale briefings are silently ignored otherwise |\n| Lean mode off / `tools.alsoAllow` | Keep spawn + wait + read tools on the coordinator's surface; a small local model may fail to *discover* a hidden tool |\n| Peer agents on other hosts | mesh send/reply with `replyTo` for explicit reply routing; broadcast only when every member is a legitimate node |\n\n**Model note:** the tutorial serves `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B`; our hot NPU model is\nthe same family, `qwen3.6-moe:35b-a3b` on\n[strixhalo](/machines/strixhalo.md) (FastFlowLM, ~8 tok/s decode). Its serving\nlane (vLLM + MI300X, ROCm) is not ours \u2014 treat the tutorial's commands as\nillustrative, and the pattern as the durable part. A low-throughput local node is\nan argument *for* fan-out (parallel specialists) and *against* long serial\ncontext.\n\n# Why the owner adopted this\n\n- It supplies the missing vocabulary for what this platform already does\n  piecemeal: supervisor + specialists, isolated nodes, artifact handoff.\n- It is the software analogue of the hardware concept in\n  [Agents on silicon](/references/agents-on-silicon.md).\n- Its central claim \u2014 *a single signal is not always sufficient* \u2014 is the same\n  failure mode the engine work keeps hitting (one metric looking healthy while\n  the real defect is silent; see [NPU A/B yardstick](/references/npu-ab-yardstick.md)\n  and [engine layering](/references/engine-layering-and-lemonade-scope.md)).\n\n# Verification status\n\nDoctrine adopted 2026-09-11 by explicit owner instruction; the source document\nwas read in full. **Not yet exercised end-to-end as a graph on this platform**:\nno run to date has used the explicit coordinator + N-specialist + one-retry\nshape with bound per-node artifacts. Until that exists, treat the mapping table\nas the operating instruction and the reliability claims (spawn-before-yield,\nsingle-retry termination) as unverified here.\n\n# See also\n\n- [Graph engineering \u2014 the source tutorial](/references/graph-engineering-openclaw-triage.md)\n- [Agents on silicon](/references/agents-on-silicon.md)\n- [Code intelligence](/policies/code-intelligence.md) \u2014 the never-do rules for the engine repo", "policies/strixhalo-driver-plan": "# Problem\n\nUbuntu 26.04 ships full ROCm 7 in its own repos (`libamdhip64-7`,\n`hipcc-rocm`, `clang-rocm`, \u2026). **Nothing is held** (`apt-mark showhold` is\nempty), so agents/updates can re-install ROCm 7 over the self-contained\nTheRock install at `/opt/rocm-therock`.\n\n# Verdict\n\n**Leave Ubuntu for Arch (plain Arch; Omarchy optional)** on\n[strixhalo](/machines/strixhalo.md):\n\n1. Ubuntu's `libamdhip64-7` / `hipcc-rocm` packages don't exist in Arch's\n   repos \u2014 nothing to auto-pull.\n2. `/opt` is outside pacman's tree \u2014 TheRock and XRT stay untouchable.\n3. No `unattended-upgrades`; updates are explicit (Omarchy even blocks raw\n   `pacman -Syu`).\n4. The NPU depends on TheRock anyway (vanilla ROCm lacks the `aie2p` agent),\n   so the self-contained `/opt` install is exactly what pacman can't clobber.\n\n# Measured baseline (2026-08-21)\n\n- TheRock ROCm at `/opt/rocm-therock` \u2014 `rocminfo` sees `gfx1151` + `aie2p`/`RyzenAI-npu5`; `hipconfig` 7.16.26332\n  (re-measured on the box 2026-09-19; historical note \u2014 the original 2026-08-21 baseline read 7.16.26331).\n- XRT 2.21.75 \u2014 `xrt-smi examine` sees `RyzenAI-npu5 @ c6:00.1`, firmware 1.1.2.65, `amdxdna` in kernel 7.0.0-30.\n- Collision source = Ubuntu's own repos (no AMD/ROCm third-party repo configured).", "references/agents-on-silicon": "# Agents on silicon (device concept)\n\nProduct/architecture brainstorm record (2026-09-08). **Status: draft concept \u2014\nno hardware bought, no repo, no BOM committed.** The idea: instead of selling\na *single offline device with one big model*, sell a device that is a\n**supervisor + six small efficient agents**, where \"agents on silicon\"\nbecomes the product framing (licensed agent SKUs, not a model in a box).\n\nCredibility comes from platform assets that already exist \u2014 the\n[1bit engine](/components/1bit-engine.md) (one binary, NPU/GPU/CPU backends),\nthe proven [strixhalo](/machines/strixhalo.md) NPU context pools, the\n[Sherry 1.25-bit ternary format](/references/sherry-format.md), and\n[JARVIS](/components/jarvis.md) as a working voice-agent pipeline prototype.\n\n## Design questions the brainstorm started from\n\n1. Goal is *not* a single offline device with one big model \u2014 it is a device\n   with several smaller FPGAs, each loaded with an agent. Sell **agents on\n   silicon** (agent = SKU-ized bundle: runtime + weights + personality +\n   license, bound to hardware).\n2. Rejected framing: a multi-model-on-a-chip monolith. Chosen framing:\n   **supervisor + small efficient agents** (agreed 2026-09-08).\n3. Constraint surfaced during the session: the small agents still need\n   *reasoning*, not just pattern matching \u2014 small/cheap and can-reason pull\n   against each other on any single die.\n\n## Decided architecture \u2014 three silicon layers\n\n| Layer | Role | Silicon home (recommended) |\n|---|---|---|\n| Supervisor brain | Big-model orchestration + open-ended reasoning; sleeps most of the time | AMD Ryzen AI (Strix-Halo-class; strixhalo = dev reference) |\n| Six specialists | Bounded, fast, always-on agent roles; each an isolated execution context | XDNA NPU hardware contexts on the same APU (see below) |\n| Trust + power plane | Signed-SKU verification, key management, anti-rollback, policy guard on separate die; audio wake path | Small FPGA (Lattice MachXO3D for trust; iCE40UP5K/MCU for wake) |\n\nKey stance: **do not buy six FPGAs for the agents.** Run the six agents as\nNPU contexts \u2014 isolation semantics already proven on strixhalo (see\n[NPU context pools](#why-npu-contexts--not-six-fpgas)). FPGA silicon earns\nexactly the trust plane and the micro-watt wake plane.\n\n## The six specialist roles\n\n| # | Agent | Function | Model class (exists in the catalog today) | Reasoning tier |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Ears | Always-on wake word + streaming ASR front end | whisper-tiny/micro VAD | none (front end) |\n| 2 | Memory | Embeddings + local vector store over the user's data; retrieval only | nomic-embed-text-v1-GGUF (lemonade) | none |\n| 3 | Voice | Local neural TTS with saved clone | piper-class / ZONOS2-1-bit | none |\n| 4 | Guard | Independent moderation/policy/sanitization, both directions (in to supervisor, out to user); must be a **separate die** from the supervisor to be a real second opinion | tiny classifier / qwen3:0.6b | shallow |\n| 5 | Eyes | OCR/vision for docs, receipts, QR (optional card) | qwen2.5vl-it:3b / MiniCPM | bounded |\n| 6 | Worker | The swappable SKU slot: tools, planning, per-customer domain | qwen3-tk:4b / deepseek-r1:8b (reasoning!) | bounded reasoning |\n\nThe supervisor is **not** the router: Ears/Memory handle routine traffic and\nonly escalate the hard 20% (Guard-sanitized) to the supervisor. Supervisor\nwakes for a brief burst, Guard re-checks the reply, Voice speaks it.\n\n## Reasoning strategy (small agents that can still reason)\n\n- **Size tiering with a reasoning floor**: sub-500M models cannot do\n  multi-step reasoning regardless of precision. Reasoning distills in the\n  1.5\u20134B class (deepseek-r1:8b, qwen3-tk:4b \u2014 both already in the FastFlowLM\n  catalog on strixhalo) handle bounded planning/tool use when aggressively\n  quantized. Worker + Guard-deep ship on a \"reasoning card\" tier, others on\n  cheap fabric.\n- **Distributed reasoning**: chain-of-thought as inter-agent hops. Worker\n  reasons one step at a time and writes intermediates to Memory's scratchpad\n  (structured, addressable), reading back only local context \u2192 each hop stays\n  within small-model context limits.\n- **Test-time compute on fabric**: parallel Worker instances at different\n  seeds/temperatures (cheap on FPGA/NPU parallelism), Guard scores\n  candidates, best wins \u2014 self-consistency buys reasoning with time/fabric,\n  not parameters.\n- **Boundary**: bounded reasoning lives in Worker; open-ended reasoning\n  (novel problems, ambiguity, long-horizon) escalates to the supervisor.\n\n## Hardware recommendation (grounded in platform facts)\n\n| Need | Choice | Why / evidence |\n|---|---|---|\n| Supervisor dev box | strixhalo (Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 128 GB UMA) | Already serves Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K via FastFlowLM ~8 tok/s |\n| Product brain module | Ryzen AI MAX or AI 300-series (\"Krackan\") APU, \u226516 GB | Weight budget is the real cost lever: 35B-A3B in [Sherry](/references/sherry-format.md) 1.25-bit ternary \u2248 7\u20139 GB \u2192 fits a cheap 16 GB unified part |\n| Six agents | XDNA NPU contexts on that APU, via the 1bit engine | amdxdna: 64 context objects / 16 concurrent exec proven; SKU/signing infrastructure scope: slot standard, manifest schema, update/attestation flow.\n\n## Related\n\n- [1bit engine](/components/1bit-engine.md) \u2014 inference engine (one binary, any backend)\n- [JARVIS](/components/jarvis.md) \u2014 voice pipeline prototype (mic \u2192 VAD \u2192 STT \u2192 LLM \u2192 TTS)\n- [strixhalo](/machines/strixhalo.md) \u2014 supervisor dev reference (Ryzen AI MAX+ 395)\n- [Sherry format](/references/sherry-format.md) \u2014 1.25-bit ternary; the weight-format cost lever\n- [Lemonade Server](/components/lemonade-server.md) \u2014 local-AI server; embedding/small-model host\n- [Strixhalo MCP](/components/strixhalo-mcp.md) \u2014 live local inference (35B chat + nomic embeddings)", "references/aie-kernel-opt-checklist": "# AIE kernel optimisation \u2014 upstream lever checklist (and what applies to us)\n\n**Source:** `Xilinx/mlir-aie` \u2192 `skills/aie-kernel-opt/SKILL.md` (23,283 B, `Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception`,\nread 2026-09-11). It is one of six skills upstream ships under `skills/`:\n\n| skill | what it covers |\n|---|---|\n| `aie-model-baseline` | locking a quantisation scheme, ONNX export, the **numeric oracle** |\n| `aie-code-creator` | IRON Python designs + C++ AIE kernels for XDNA (AIE2/AIE2P: Phoenix/Hawk/Strix/Krackan) |\n| `aie-dataflow-presim` | pre-hardware validation: threaded ObjectFifo/Worker mock, FIFO depth/deadlock, bit-exact vs oracle |\n| `aie-hw-bringup` | block-by-block first bring-up on real hardware against the oracle |\n| `aie-dataflow-opt` | **macro**: dispatch partitioning, tile placement, streaming, DMA bandwidth |\n| `aie-kernel-opt` | **micro**: make one compiled kernel faster (this file) |\n\nUpstream frames all six as *demonstration* material \u2014 \"provided as-is with no guarantees of support\". Apache-2.0\nWITH LLVM-exception, so vendoring is licence-clean (unlike the third-party repo reviewed the same day, which had no\nlicence at all).\n\n## Method (measure first \u2014 do not skip)\n\n`baseline \u2192 bit-exact gate \u2192 ablation \u2192 verify in the .o`. The *bit-exact gate* is the same discipline as our\nadmissibility fixture: a change is only comparable if the comparison is valid. The **verify-in-.o** step is exactly\nhow the `.bss` regression was found (see #2199 and `build_p1i4.sh`'s lint): read the compiled object, do not infer\ncodegen from the source.\n\n**Before any of it**, the sibling `aie-dataflow-opt` skill asks the prior question \u2014 *is this kernel on the critical\npath at all?* (its lever #1 is a NOOP ablation). Optimising a kernel that is not the bottleneck is the most common\nway to spend a week for nothing.\n\n## The nine levers, in priority order\n\n1. **Loop hints** \u2014 cheapest, often the biggest. Include `aie_kernel_utils.h`, decorate every non-trivial loop. The\n   macro goes **before** the `for`, never inside the parens.\n2. **Compile-time shapes and trip counts** \u2014 the lever that unlocks the others; Peano optimises far more\n   aggressively when bounds/strides/shapes are constants.\n3. **Kill `__divsi3` / signed power-of-2 ops on the hot path** \u2014 `a / 8` \u2260 `a >> 3` for negatives, so it lowers to\n   a library call.\n4. **No branches inside the inner compute loop** \u2014 a per-iteration branch blocks back-to-back `vld+vld+vmac` issue.\n5. **Vectorise the epilogue** (bias + requantise/SRS + clamp + activation) \u2014 the scalar tail becomes the bottleneck\n   once the inner loop is tight.\n6. **Pre-pack operand layout** \u2014 the scalar gather feeding `mmul` is frequently the real cost.\n7. **Pack wide copies explicitly** \u2014 write the wide move rather than hoping a byte loop is widened.\n8. **Wider `mmul` shape** \u2014 only where it amortises; check the aie-api headers for the target's actual widths.\n9. **Move pure data movement into DMA** \u2014 a kernel body that is only a strided copy/transpose/deinterleave can free\n   a whole tile.\n\n## Two caveats that decide whether a lever can work here at all\n\n**(a) `aie_kernel_utils.h`'s macros are inert unless one of two macros is defined.** The header has three branches:\n\n| condition | what the macros become |\n|---|---|\n| `__chess__` | chess pragmas (`[[chess::unroll_loop(x)]]`, \u2026) |\n| `__AIECC__` | clang pragmas (`_Pragma(\"clang loop unroll_count(x)\")`, \u2026) |\n| **neither** | **nothing at all** \u2014 every macro expands to empty (`#else`) |\n\nOur kernels are compiled by a **direct** `$P/bin/clang++ --target=aie2p-none-unknown-elf`, and **nothing in our build\nmachinery defines `__AIECC__`** (checked across `engine/npu/**/*.sh` and the generators). So today: six kernels\ninclude the header, **none of them uses any of its macros**, and if one did, `AIE_LOOP_UNROLL(...)` would expand to\nnothing \u2014 a silent no-op. Applying lever 1 therefore requires passing `-D__AIECC__` or compiling the TU through\n`aiecc`, and the *absence* of the enablement looks exactly like \"the hint did not help\".\n\n**(b) The chess branch is not available on this box.** `xchesscc_wrapper` is a symlink to itself (ELOOP), `aietools`\nis absent, and our compiler A/B records that the chess arm writes zeros on hardware (#1878). So the `__AIECC__`\n(clang/Peano) branch is the only viable one here.\n\n## Our kernels against the greppable levers (scan 2026-09-11, `engine/npu/kernel/*.cc`)\n\n| file | includes header | `AIE_LOOP` uses | for-loops | `mmul` | `/const` on ints |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| edge_attention_06b_compact.cc | \u2013 | 0 | 11 | 0 | 0 |\n| edge_attention.cc | \u2013 | 0 | 11 | 0 | 0 |\n| full_vector_station_06b.cc | \u2013 | 0 | 6 | 0 | 0 |\n| mm_binary_q1.cc | yes | 0 | 7 | 0 | 0 |\n| mm_ternary_stq_aie2.cc | yes | 0 | 15 | 5 | 0 |\n| mm_ternary_tq1.cc | yes | 0 | 13 | 0 | 0 |\n| mm_ternary_tq2_aie2.cc | yes | 0 | 20 | 4 | 0 |\n| mm_ternary_tq2.cc | yes | 0 | 11 | 0 | 0 |\n| postprocess_qkv_06b.cc | \u2013 | 0 | 9 | 0 | 0 |\n| qwen3_decode_kernels_06b.cc | \u2013 | 0 | 4 | 0 | 0 |\n| ssm_selective_scan.cc | yes | 0 | 4 | 0 | 0 |\n| test_stq_gemv_ref.cc | \u2013 | 0 | 30 | 2 | 0 |\n| test_tq2_gemv_ref.cc | \u2013 | 0 | 21 | 3 | 0 |\n| swiglu_06b.cc | \u2013 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 |\n\nFindings:\n\n- **Lever 1 is entirely un-applied: 14 kernels, 0 `AIE_LOOP*` uses**, six of which already include the header. This is\n  the cheapest available lever and the most obviously unconsumed \u2014 but see caveat (a) before expecting a delta.\n- **Lever 3 does not apply to us.** No `__divsi3` in any in-tree object or listing, and no integer `/const` on the\n  kernel paths. Recorded so nobody hunts for it.\n- **Lever 8 applies to four files only** (`mm_ternary_stq_aie2`, `mm_ternary_tq2_aie2`, `test_stq_gemv_ref`,\n  `test_tq2_gemv_ref`) \u2014 everywhere else there is no `mmul` to widen, which raises the dataflow-opt question of\n  whether those kernels should be using the matrix unit at all.\n- The attention kernels (`edge_attention*.cc`, 11 for-loops each, no `mmul`, no hints) are the most lever-rich\n  candidates; upstream's skill explicitly covers \"INT8 conv, matmul, attention, elementwise\".\n\n**Order of work if this is ever picked up:** establish the bottleneck first (`aie-dataflow-opt`'s NOOP ablation),\nthen enable the header's macro branch (`-D__AIECC__`) so the hints are not silently dropped, then lever 1, then the\nshapes (lever 2) which unlocks the rest \u2014 with the bit-exact gate and a `.o` inspection at every step.", "references/amdgcn-gfx1151": "# What this is\n\nThe hard-won knowledge from hand-writing AMDGCN kernels on this specific\ntarget. Ground truth is empirical \u2014 verified by running kernels on the real\nGPU \u2014 not from ISA docs.\n\n# The ABI contract (what a hand-written kernel must respect)\n\n- **s[0:1]** = kernarg segment pointer (user SGPR, `amdhsa_user_sgpr_count 2`\n  + `amdhsa_user_sgpr_kernarg_segment_ptr 1`).\n- **s[2:3]** = workgroup_id_x (system SGPR); **v0** = workitem_id_x\n  (provided by the HW; do NOT use `v_mbcnt` \u2014 see broken list).\n- Kernarg layout: **user args at offsets 0..**, hidden args after (clang\n  kernels put block dim etc. at 0x24+; we declare none and read only ours).\n- Kernel descriptor (`amdhsa_kernel` directives) + the **`.amdgpu_metadata`\n  YAML block are both required** \u2014 the YAML becomes the `.note` section the\n  loader parses. Missing it \u2192 kernel not found.\n- Code object must be **ET_DYN** (link `-shared`) \u2014 HSA rejects ET_REL.\n\n# AQL dispatch packet (hand-rolled)\n\n- `setup` = **dimensions (1/2/3)** \u2014 NOT zero-based (`setup=0` \u2192\n  `INCOMPATIBLE_ARGUMENTS`).\n- **`grid_size_x` = TOTAL workitems, not block count** \u2014 the hardware\n  divides by workgroup size to make blocks. (This one cost the most\n  debugging time.)\n- `workgroup_size_y/z` and `grid_size_y/z` must be \u2265 1.\n- Queue min size **64**; private/group segment hints = `UINT32_MAX`.\n- **Completion signal: never touch it** \u2014 the HW decrements it; arm it to 1\n  and wait for `< 1`. Re-arm with `store_relaxed(1)` between dispatches.\n- Buffers must come from a memory pool (`hsa_amd_memory_pool_allocate`,\n  fine-grained pool) \u2014 plain `malloc`'d host memory **faults on the GPU**.\n- Kernels are registered under the symbol **`<name>.kd`**; `get_symbol`\n  misses PROTECTED symbols \u2014 iterate symbols and match the name.\n- Launch: `hsa_queue_create(agent, 64, HSA_QUEUE_TYPE_SINGLE, ..., UINT32_MAX, UINT32_MAX, &q)`.\n\n# Broken / surprising on this target (verified)\n\n| Item | Observation |\n|---|---|\n| `hipModuleLoad` / `hipModuleLoadData` | **Segfault** on external .co in TheRock HIP 7.16 \u2014 use the HSA API directly |\n| `v_dot2_f32_f16` | **Computes 0** (assembles, executes, silent zero) \u2014 verified in a 5-line HIP micro-test |\n| `v_mbcnt_lo_u32_b32` | Returns 0 for all lanes on gfx1151 \u2014 use the HW-provided workitem id in v0 |\n| `s_mul_lo_u32` / `v_mac_f32` / `v_mad_f32` | Not valid on gfx1151 \u2014 use `v_mul_lo_u32` / `v_fma_f32` |\n| `global_load_b16` | Name is `global_load_u16` on this assembler |\n| VOPC dest register | Must be **`vcc_lo`** (wave32) \u2014 `vcc` / `s[6:7]` rejected |\n| VOPC operands | SGPR/literal src rejected \u2014 move bounds into VGPRs first |\n| old.reddit.com | Login-walled \u2014 Reddit JSON via Camoufox instead (see [camoufox](/components/camoufox.md)) |\n\n# The toolchain (strixhalo)\n\n- `amdclang` at `/opt/rocm-therock/bin` (clang 23.0.0git), `hipcc` 7.16.\n- SDK layout: `/opt/rocm-therock/lib/python3.14/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel`\n  (`include/`, `lib/`, `lib/llvm/bin/llvm-objdump`).\n- Assemble: `amdclang --target=amdgcn-amd-amdhsa -mcpu=gfx1151 -shared -fPIC k.s -o k.hsaco`.\n\n# Verified\n\nEvery row above was hit and worked around live on 2026-08-26 while building\nthe [kernel lab](/components/kernel-lab.md) kernels (vecadd PASS on 16.7M\nelements; TQ2 GEMV 0/6912 vs CPU ref).", "references/chess-arg-delivery-defect": "# Chess kernel arm: no base pointers are delivered (issue #1878, re-measured 2026-09-11)\n\n> **CORRECTION (2026-09-11, after reading upstream #3690): this defect is already SOLVED, and the\n> \"blocked\" conclusion below is withdrawn.** The root cause and a verified fix were recorded in\n> [Xilinx/mlir-aie#3690](https://github.com/Xilinx/mlir-aie/issues/3690) \u2014 *filed four days earlier by\n> our own account* \u2014 whose final comment is titled \"RESOLVED: root cause = the guarded acquire\".\n>\n> * **Root cause**: the Vitis 2025.2/2026.1 **aie2ps** chess models expose only the **guarded**\n>   acquire intrinsic (`chessintr_void_acquire_guarded` \u2192 `30 18 12 20`). A core stuck on that guarded\n>   acquire never completes on NPU2 (`ERT_CMD_STATE_TIMEOUT`), while the DMA/design side uses the plain\n>   protocol.\n> * **Working configuration**: compile chess kernels with the **Ryzen-AI 1.3.0 `vitis_aie_essentials`\n>   (2024)** aie2p chess (plain `acq`, `18 18 12 10`), and link cores through the **peano path**\n>   (`--xchesscc --no-xbridge`, 2024 essentials `xchesscc` on PATH) with `me_primitive` stubs +\n>   `libsoftfloat.a` for f32 conversions. Toolchain is on strixhalo at\n>   `~/Downloads/ryzen_ai-1.3.0/vitis_aie_essentials/bin/xchesscc`.\n> * **Verified 2026-09-07 on strixhalo**: IRON `axpy` 20/20 and `silu` 20/20 with `--compiler chess`;\n>   peano regression clean.\n>\n> Everything measured in this record used the **2026.1 chess + `--xbridge`** configuration \u2014 the one\n> #3690 identifies as hung. So the measurements are **corroboration from the host-visible side**, not a\n> new defect: a core that never progresses past its guarded acquire never calls the kernel, which is\n> exactly why no kernel argument and not even an absolute store was ever observable here.\n>\n> The lesson is in [the log](../log.md): re-deriving a defect from scratch, with the known-hung\n> configuration, reproduced a symptom our own upstream issue had already resolved.\n\n## Symptom\n\n`engine/npu/tests/bench_compiler_ab.sh` \u2014 same kernel, same MLIR design, same harness, **only the\nkernel `.o` compiler differs** \u2014 reproduces the recorded result on a clean `origin/main` worktree:\n\n```\npeano  PASS  7.706 ms \u00b7 557.3 GOP/s     pass 0 and pass 1 both clean\nchess  FAIL  pass 0: min=0 max=0 wrong=1048576/1048576 zero=1048576\n```\n\nThe chess arm builds, links, loads and executes; the output buffer is never written. The bench gates\non correctness, so a broken arm yields FAIL and no timing.\n\n## The measured chain\n\n1. **The chess toolchain works.** With chess-native flags (`-c -O2 -DNDEBUG -D__AIE_API_AIE_ADF_HPP__`\n   and includes) plus the license environment and the Vitis launcher first on `PATH`, a compile exits 0\n   and produces a valid object. Passing *peano* flags (`-std=`, `--target=`) fails with\n   `Invalid option` \u2014 the harness already knows this (\"chess rejects `-std=` entirely\").\n2. **The ABI symbol is fine.** Both objects export the same global entry `T matmul_i8_i32`, so the\n   design binds the same symbol in both arms.\n3. **The instruction streams are byte-identical** between arms (`insts_*.txt`, 514,320 B each,\n   `cmp` clean) \u2014 the host-side/DMA delivery and parameters are the same in both xclbins.\n4. **The working arm's delivery is a visible instruction.** In the peano core program\n   (`main_core_0_2.elf`, 4,416 B) the kernel's arguments are placed as\n   `movs p0, r0 ; mov p1, r1` immediately before `jl <kernel>` \u2014 three call sites, three occurrences.\n5. **The chess core program contains that instruction zero times** \u2014 not the exact 8-byte op\n   (`027050b000600110`) and not even its 4-byte opcode prefix (`027050b0`), against 3 occurrences in\n   peano's. The chess core program is 59,836 B with byte entropy 4.84 (real code, not padding), so this\n   is a *different core program*, not the same one with metadata attached.\n6. **A chess object cannot be linked by the peano flow at all:**\n   ```\n   ld.lld: error: mm_32x64x128.o:(.tctmemtab) is being placed in '.tctmemtab'\n   ld.lld: error: \u2026(.rtstab) / (.eoltab) / (.chesstypeannotationtab)\n   \u2192 Error linking core (0, 2)\n   ```\n   Those sections are exactly what `--xbridge` exists to translate: the chess object carries\n   `.tctmemtab` (0x70), `.rtstab` (0x222), `.eoltab` (0x1638) and `.chesstypeannotationtab` (0x890) \u2014\n   its own runtime tables, i.e. **chess delivers kernel arguments through a mechanism the peano path\n   does not use**. The peano flow's register delivery never happens in the chess flow.\n\n## What is ruled out (each measured, not assumed)\n\n| hypothesis | status |\n|---|---|\n| a newer `xchesscc` fixes it | **ruled out here** \u2014 the launcher maps `--aiearch aie2p` to `tps/lnx64/target_aie2p` = `#764cd94af1#260213` (2026-02-13). The newer `#865883355f#260312` (2026-03-13) sits in `tps/lnx64/target/`, which `aie2p` never sources. All per-target binaries carry the 2026-06-16 install date. |\n| wrong compile flags | **ruled out** \u2014 chess-native flags compile cleanly, exit 0. |\n| an ABI knob on the compiler | **none exists** \u2014 `xchesscc --help` has no calling-convention/register option. |\n| our kernel source | **not the cause** \u2014 the same source compiles in both arms. (An earlier version of this record claimed an *ABI mismatch* \u2014 peano reading `p0, p1` and chess `p0, p2`. **That claim is withdrawn:** it came from a grep for `mov reg, pN`, which cannot see pointers used directly in addressing modes (`vldb x0, [p1], #0x40`), and a control settles it \u2014 with simple pointer signatures chess allocates `p0, p1` (2 args) and `p0, p1, p2` (3 args), i.e. normally. The ABI is not shown to differ; the **delivery** is what differs.) |\n| a kernel-source shim can fix it | **ruled out for the naive form** \u2014 with no argument-delivery instruction in the chess core program and no readable disassembly of it (`llvm-objdump` asserts: `AIE2PGenAsmWriter: Cannot print this instruction`), there is no register to read in compensation. |\n\n## Impact\n\n- **Chess is unusable for the tracked NPU kernel set**, so the shipped xclbins stay peano-built, and\n  `PROVENANCE.json`'s `toolchain: null` remains honest \u2014 see\n  [NPU xclbin artifact provenance](/references/npu-xclbin-provenance.md) \u00a77c for the rebuild blockers\n  that sit alongside this one.\n- The defect is in **aiecc's `--xchesscc --xbridge` core-program generation / chess runtime-table\n  delivery**, not in the kernel source, the flags, the version, or the design.\n\n## Workaround options\n\n1. ~~**Signature padding**~~ \u2014 **dead, by control.** It assumed chess allocates arguments to\n   `p0, p2, \u2026` skipping `p1`; measured, chess allocates `p0, p1` (2 args) and `p0, p1, p2` (3 args),\n   normally. There is no register to pad *to*, so this option is withdrawn rather than left as a\n   promising idea.\n2. ~~**Stay on peano** and treat chess as blocked until upstream fixes it.~~ **Withdrawn** \u2014 chess is not blocked; see the correction at the top: the 2024-era essentials chess with `--xchesscc --no-xbridge` runs (IRON axpy/silu 20/20), and the 2026.1 + `--xbridge` configuration used here is the known-hung one.\n3. **Report upstream**: the repro above is minimal and unambiguous \u2014 identical instruction streams, the\n   peano delivery op present 3\u00d7 and absent 0\u00d7 in the chess core program, the link-section errors, and\n   the all-zeros result.\n\n## Reproduce\n\n```bash\n# on strixhalo, in a worktree at a clean ref (a dirty working tree gives a failing peano arm too)\ngit worktree add --detach /tmp/ab origin/main && cd /tmp/ab\nbash engine/npu/tests/bench_compiler_ab.sh --rounds 1 --iters 20 --keep\n#   -> peano PASS, chess FAIL all-zeros\nllvm-objdump -d --triple=aie2p .../peano/design.mlir.prj/main_core_0_2.elf | grep 'movs p0'\n#   -> the delivery op before each jl <kernel>\npython3 -c \"print(open('.../chess/design.mlir.prj/main_core_0_2.elf','rb').read().count(bytes.fromhex('027050b000600110')))\"\n#   -> 0\n```\n\n## What chess's own tooling shows (read 2026-08, strixhalo)\n\nChess ships its own inspection tools and its own listing, which decodes what `llvm-objdump` refuses\nto. This is the only surface that lets the *delivery* be read at all.\n\n**Artifacts**: `design.mlir.prj/main_core_<r>_<c>.elf.lst` (6,642 lines, 418 KB) \u2014 chess's own\ndisassembly listing; alongside `.map` (link map), `.calltree`, `.cmic2`/`.cmico`, `.sdr`, `.srv`,\n`.bcf` \u2014 i.e. the runtime/argument metadata that the peano flow does not produce.\n\n**What the listing establishes**\n\n1. Chess lowers the design to LLVM IR first, then **links the kernel in with `chess-llvm-link`**\n   (`design.mlir.prj/main_input.chesshack.ll` \u2192 `main_input.chesslinked.ll`). Verified by running\n   aiecc with `-v` and reading the command it issues.\n2. **The IR is identical between arms.** `main_input.ll` for peano and chess are both 3,390 lines\n   and agree at the call site \u2014 same declaration `declare void @matmul_i8_i32(ptr, ptr, ptr)`, same\n   call with three pointers, output last. So design, descriptors, arguments and call are *not* the\n   difference. (The `inttoptr (i64 3735928559 to ptr)` = `0xDEADBEEF` sentinel near the call is a\n   benign never-taken phi input: it occurs **64 times in *both* arms**.)\n3. **The kernel's contract is `p0`/`p1`/`p2`** \u2014 the kernel body dereferences `[p0]` 63\u00d7, `[p1]`\n   33\u00d7, `[p2]` 32\u00d7. Same three-pointer contract the IR expresses.\n4. **Chess's delivery is memory-based, not register-based.** Chess references an argument block via\n   `p6`/`p7`: `LDA p0, [p6], #\u2026` (listing line 37), `LDA r17, [p6], #4`, `LDA r19, [p6]`,\n   `LDA r17, [p7, #4]`, and saves/restores them with `LDA p6, [sp, #\u2026]` / `LDA p7, [sp, #\u2026]`.\n   Peano instead delivers by register (`movs p0, r0; mov p1, r1`). **The two compilers implement\n   different argument-delivery mechanisms**, which is why the byte pattern that delivers in the\n   peano core program is absent from the chess one.\n5. **In the caller `core_0_2`, the delivery is not visible** \u2014 there is no `LDA p0/p1/p2` anywhere in\n   that function, only `LDA r17/r19, [p6]/[p7]` (scalar reads from the block) and the lock\n   operations (`MOVA r0, #52/#49/#48/#53`, matching `llvm.aie2p.acquire` in the IR).\n\n**The wall (precise)**\n\nSeveral instructions in the caller are **undecoded in the vendor's own listing** \u2014 raw hex with no\nmnemonic, 4\u20136 bytes each, at addresses 368, 374, 462, 476, 498, 516, 578, 650.
