They\nare about *derived* artifacts \u2014 censuses, manifests, bundles, fixtures \u2014 where the artifact states something\nabout a tree, a build or a run rather than being it.\n\n**Citation convention.** Numbers are local to this document (rules 1-6); `machines/strixhalo.md` runs its own sequence 6-11, and \"rule 6\" alone would be ambiguous. Both lists carry names, so cross-document citations use the name \u2014 \"split invariant from variant\" here, \"name the revision\" there \u2014 and `<document> rule N` is reserved for when a number is specifically wanted.\n\n## 1. Anchor the ref, and make the copy carry it\n\nA derived artifact records **`ref` + `generator` + `timestamp`**, and consumers **quote the anchor** rather\nthan restating numbers.\n\n**A hash is evidence about the moment it was taken.** `sha256sum` of a *moving* file \u2014 `log.md`, a branch tip, a live\ncensus \u2014 is stale by construction as soon as it is quoted later, and it reads as a present-tense claim. Attach the\nmoment (`log.md = e4aaef8dd07c6fb6 @ 2026-09-11T18:0xZ`) or quote the artifact that pins the content (`SOURCE_REV` +\n`MANIFEST.sha256`). Tonight produced two defects of this shape in one hour \u2014 a log hash quoted as current, and an\n\"okf is in sync\" inference drawn from two equal tips \u2014 and neither was a measurement error.\n\nTwo independent inventions of the same mechanism, which is the argument for it being standard shape:\n\n- `engine/npu/xclbins/PROVENANCE.json` \u2192 `generated.ref: ef8c0cdf9` (PR #2211);\n- the determinism bundle \u2192 `SOURCE_REV: <okf rev>` (`~/npu-determinism/SOURCE_REV`).\n\nWhy it matters, measured: the same census published **23.40%** (on `feat/hrx-gfx1151-build 05511bb51`) and\n**23.34%** (on `origin/main ef8c0cdf9`) with an *identical numerator* \u2014 one file,\n`final_i8_GUSILU_i4_qwen3_0_6b_bf16pair.xclbin`, is 77,424 B vs 101,280 B (**+23,856 B**), and\n`final_i8_MOE_FUSED_zaya.xclbin` is the same size on both refs but differs in content (its embedded AXLF\n`TimeStamp`, which also moves the day histogram from 16 to 18 UTC days).\n\n**The reader needs the ref, not just the writer.** An anchor only helps if the copy carries it \u2014 a figure\nrestated in a summary, a description or a chat message without its ref is unreproducible even when it was\nmeasured correctly.\n\n## 2. Exclude yourself explicitly\n\nAn artifact that **counts or hashes its own container** must state the exclusion, or its value depends on\nwhether the artifact has landed in the tree. Two instances, identical repair:\n\n| artifact | defect | repair |\n|---|---|---|\n| `~/npu-determinism/MANIFEST.sha256` | listed **its own hash**, so `sha256sum -c` was *guaranteed* red \u2014 and a permanently-red check hides real corruption as the expected output | generate with `! -name MANIFEST.sha256` |\n| `PROVENANCE.json` | `population.tracked_paths_under_dir: 510`, while the checker prints **511** on a checkout containing the manifest \u2014 it counts itself | exclude it, or say \"excluding this manifest\" |\n\n## 3. Split invariant from variant \u2014 the strongest form\n\nWhen a summary mixes quantities, **quote the ref-invariant subset**: that removes the need for a ref\nentirely, which is stronger than adding one.\n\nWorked example from the xclbin census:\n\n| quantity | ref-invariant? |\n|---|---|\n| 127 top-level paths \u00b7 111 regular AXLF artifacts \u00b7 16 symlinks (12 aliases + 4 dangling) \u00b7 86 distinct by `XclBinUUID` \u00b7 25 byte-identical duplicate pairs \u00b7 **2,226,430 B redundant** | **yes** \u2014 identical on both refs (the checker computes 2,226,430 on the PR tree; the manifest records 2,226,430 for `ef8c0cdf9`) | \u2014 **observed 2026-09-11 pre-#2218**; #2218 (open, armed) deletes the 4 dangling aliases, so the merged population is 123/111/12/24/86 |\n| payload total (9,513,667 vs 9,537,523 B) and therefore the percentage (23.40% vs 23.34%) | **no** \u2014 moved by that one file |\n\nSo the frontmatter `description` can state the duplicate structure with no ref at all, leaving the payload\nand the percentage to the two labelled `ref` blocks. A summary line that needs no ref is the goal; one that\nmerely has a ref attached is the fallback.\n\nCorollary for prose \u2014 **and this is the condition that makes it safe: an approximation is invariant only if its\nprecision is coarser than the ref-to-ref spread.** \"Approximation\" alone confers nothing; the tilde is not what\nmakes a number invariant. Worked counter-example from the same table:\n\n| quoted as | refs 23.40% / 23.34% (spread **0.06 pp**) | invariant? |\n|---|---|---|\n| `~23.4%` (1 dp) | rounds to 23.4 vs 23.3 | **no** \u2014 it is the HRX value wearing a tilde |\n| `~23%` (0 dp) | 23 vs 23 | **yes** |\n| `~9.5 MB` (1 dp) | 9,513,667 and 9,537,523 B, spread 0.0239 MB | **yes** \u2014 the rounding window is far wider |\n\nSo the same cell can be half right and half wrong: the MB half invariant, the percentage half not. **Precision is\ntherefore a rule-6 parameter**, alongside field, root, timezone, population, unit, scope, `n` and ref \u2014 and the\nlast of them to be named.\n\nCorollary for *which* field carries it: the frontmatter `title` is what an index or a search surfaces, so it is\nwhere a ref-free variant figure does the most damage. Invariant fragments there (`86 builds behind 127 paths`,\n`4 committed dangling links`) can stay; a variant figure must be coarsened to an invariant precision or dropped.\n\n**And a length is a claim about a unit.** One paragraph quoted `3,583` and `3,589` for the same file: the first\nwas a **character** count (`len()` in the language that wrote it), the second a **byte** count (`stat -c%s`), and\nthe file's three non-ASCII `\u2014` characters make the two differ by exactly +2 each. `len(s)` and `stat -c%s` are\ntherefore different instruments that agree only on pure ASCII \u2014 the MB-versus-MiB trap one level down, and the\nsecond unit slip of that night. When quoting a size, name the unit, or quote the byte count, since bytes are what\nthe filesystem, every hash and every diff agree on.\n\n**It is a clause rather than a correction because it was not one person's slip:** two agents hit it\nindependently within the hour, from two separate instruments, each labelling a character count as a size \u2014 and\nboth figures were in the same artifact's paragraph at the same time.\n\nBut recurrence is only **evidence**, not the test: two agents can hit the same coincidence. The test is the\nmechanism \u2014 **name the interface that made the wrong belief available.** Here the interface itself produced the\nfalse unit: a wrapper's output line printed `bytes` while computing `len()`, and `len()` and `os.path.getsize()`\nagree **only on pure ASCII**, so the wrong belief is latent in the tool until the first non-ASCII character\nappears. Demonstrated: a 20-byte ASCII string gives `len()=20` and `getsize=20`; add one em dash and it is `23`\nagainst `25`. **If an interface produces the belief, the item belongs in this list; if there is only a coincidence\nrepeated, it does not.**\n\n## Audit recipe for this bundle (and its two conditions)\n\nThe check is a grep for the variant figures across every `*.md`:\n`9,513,667|9,537,523|23.40%|23.34%|~23.4%|\u224823.4%`. Two conditions, each learned by getting it wrong:\n\n1. **Include the short ref forms** \u2014 `HRX`, `baseline`, `main` \u2014 as well as SHAs. A line that names both refs in\n   prose (`23.40% at HRX, 23.34% at the baseline`) is *correct* but scores zero against a SHA-only pattern, and a\n   pattern that under-reports looks exactly like a pass. Same sub-domain error as the quoting and version-suffix\n   traps: the pattern chose the conclusion.\n2. **Quote the matched text, not a line number.** The bundle is a *moving* file: line numbers cited in one session\n   point at different content after the next commit, and the bundle deliberately carries two logs \u2014 a repo-root\n   `log.md` and `systems/1bit-monster/log.md` \u2014 so a line number alone can send the reader to the wrong file\n   entirely. An audit should carry the string it matched.\n\n## 4. Distinguish enforced from recorded\n\nA summary of a check must name the **keys it compares**, not the values it prints. A printed number reads as a\ngate, and the error is asymmetric: an overstated gate is *trusted*, while an understated one is merely redundant.\n\nWorked example \u2014 PR #2211's `compare()`, read rather than summarised. Of four values quoted as \"CI expectations\":\n\n| value | status |\n|---|---|\n| `86` (`distinct_builds_by_uuid`) | **gated** \u2014 one of six compared population keys |\n| `4` (`declared_dangling`) | **gated**, and as an exact dict: the four paths *and* their targets must match, with messages distinguishing \"was dangling, now it RESOLVES\" from \"newly dangling\" |\n| `28` | **derivable, ungated** \u2014 16 `xclbin_symlinks` + 12 `alias_symlinks_in_tree`, both gated, but no total-symlink key is compared |\n| `~23%` (`census.redundant_percent`) | **recorded, not enforced** \u2014 `compare()` never touches `census` |\n\nTwo real, one derivable, one informational. And the strongest gate in that check is one nobody quoted: **per-UUID\n`sha256` plus alias `paths` for all 86 artifacts** \u2014 content-level, so it catches a ref change at the\nartifact-bytes level, which is exactly what anchoring the manifest to `ef8c0cdf9` buys.\n\n### The second axis: prominence and enforcement are independent\n\nA rule phrased only as \"distinguish enforced from recorded\" leaves the reader to assume the two **correlate**.\nThey do not: an artifact can label one instrument *preferred* and another *cheap* while gating only the cheap one.\nThe distinction is therefore not strong-vs-weak but **designed-for vs actually-run**.\n\nFound by applying rule 4 to the determinism bundle that produced it (`~/npu-determinism`, 2026-09-11): the value-side\ninstrument (`rvals.so` + the `fnv=` fixture table in `FIXTURES.md`) was **recorded and enforced by nothing** \u2014 a grep\nfor `fnv=` across the bundle's `*.sh` returned nothing, and `FIXTURES.md` contained zero mentions of\nenforced/recorded/gate \u2014 while the *count-side* `guard_v4.sh` was the only thing actually asserting anything. So in\nthe bundle that defined the rule, the preferred instrument was advisory and the fallback was the gate.\n\nRepair: `guard/guard_fixture.sh` now asserts the churn hash and the `engine[N]` table, fails closed when the shim is\nabsent, and carries four controls (positive on the pre-change binary, negative on a cold cache, post-change mode, and\nthe fail-closed path with no shims present). `guard_v4.sh` stays the cost-free fallback it was labelled as.\n\nCorollary: a **recorded** count may legitimately be inexact in a way a **gated** one may not. A population key that\nincludes the manifest itself is harmless when nothing compares it and a defect only when it is gated \u2014 so the\nrepair there is a documentation note, not a change to the number.\n\n## 5. Assert your own mutations on two axes\n\nEvery mutation \u2014 a commit, an edit, a file write \u2014 needs **two** assertions, because each one alone has a blind\ndirection:\n\n| axis | check | catches | blind to |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **it happened** | `before=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` **immediately before** the mutation, then `[ \"$before\" != \"$after\" ]` | a mutation that never happened: a missing `git add`, a message file that does not exist, an anchor that matched nothing | *what* landed \u2014 a commit carrying the wrong content passes |\n| **it carries the intent** | the intended bytes are in the result: `git show HEAD:<path> \\| cmp - <intended>`, or a file-hash compare (`3fc1b43f \u2192 66b6a8ba`) | a mutation that landed carrying something else: a wrapped-line anchor that silently no-op'd, a partial replace | whether it happened at all |\n\nTwo conditions, each learned by getting it wrong:\n\n- **Capture `before` immediately before the mutation, never at the top of the script.** A stale `before` makes the\n  comparison report \"moved\" for a change that never landed \u2014 the false-*positive* direction, which is worse than the\n  false negative because it is **trusted**. Both directions happened in one session: a hard-coded `before` reported\n  \"landed\" for a commit that failed, and a missing `git add` produced a silence that the same check caught.\n- **A tip move proves that *some* commit happened, not what it contains.** `TIP DID NOT MOVE` is therefore necessary\n  and not sufficient; the content assertion is the other half of the rule, not a nicety.\n- **Axis 2 is a byte comparison, not a substring search \u2014 that retires this caveat instead of documenting it.**\n  The first version grepped for the intended text and failed on case (`assert` vs a heading `Assert`), but a grep\n  inherits case, whitespace, line wrapping and encoding: the pattern-fidelity class that recurred all day (a\n  capitalised heading, a wrapped-line anchor, the `\"-I\"` shell-quoting phantom, `srand_calls=` matching inside\n  `rand_calls=`, `rand@GLIBC_2.2.5` defeating `\" rand$\"`). For the question axis 2 actually answers \u2014 *is what I meant\n  in there* \u2014 **no pattern is needed**: keep the intended content (or its `sha256`) and compare bytes\n  (`git show HEAD:<path> | cmp - <intended>`, or hash equality; `git diff --quiet HEAD -- <path>` for in-place edits).\n  That is exact, so a landed change reads as landed however it is spelled, and it removes the axis the failure lived\n  on. A substring search stays the right instrument when the intent genuinely *is* \"this phrase exists somewhere\" \u2014 a\n  documentation sweep or a cross-reference check. It is only wrong for \"my edit landed\", which is a statement about\n  bytes.\n- **The general form, which is the move worth keeping from this whole session: prefer the instrument that cannot fail\n  in the known direction over the caveat that records how it failed.** The caveat costs a reader's memory; the\n  instrument costs nothing and cannot be forgotten.\n\n### The register symmetry\n\n\"An intention reported as a result\" has three registers, all observed in one afternoon:\n\n| register | example | the repair |\n|---|---|---|\n| peer-facing | a diff described rather than written | write the file and say so |\n| artifact-facing | a commit not made (`git add` omitted, message file missing) | axis 1 above |\n| content-facing | a commit made that does not carry what was meant | axis 2 above |\n\n### The three control types, and the one that proves the generator ran\n\nPositive and negative controls show that a check discriminates; a fail-closed branch shows that it refuses when it\ncannot tell. Neither covers the case where the *thing under test did not run at all*, and that case produces a\ncomfortable pass: a cross-root comparison whose copy was never regenerated compares a file to itself, and a\ngeneration step that exited 126 (not executable) or died on a missing import leaves the previous output in place,\nwhich then \"matches\". Found on 2026-09-11 while making the okf generated tree host-independent \u2014 two harness\nfailures (exit 126 from a non-executable `site.py`, then `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'markdown'` under\nplain `python3`) each produced a *passing* cross-root test before the correct one.\n\nThe control that catches it is a **mutation the generator must erase**: write a marker into a generated artifact,\nrun the generator, and assert the marker is gone. Identical output is not evidence that a generator ran \u2014 only the\ndisappearance of something you inserted is.\n\n### Is the instrument's own report possible?\n\nA neighbour of the third control, and cheap enough to be reflex: before acting on a reading, ask whether the reading *could* be\nright. A read tool reported *\"Offset 104 is beyond end of file (1 lines total)\"* for a 145-line file immediately after a\nsuccessful edit \u2014 a claim falsifiable in one command (`wc -l`), and the recovery was to **measure with a different\ninstrument** rather than to re-read with, or argue with, the first one. (`wc -l` and `grep` both showed the file intact.)\n\nThis is the truncation family from the other side: those were instruments that discarded part of the truth, this one\ninvented a fact. In both, the fix is a second measurement rather than more confidence in the first, and a report that is\nimpossible in principle is the one case where the right response is to disbelieve without checking further \u2014 but only\nbecause one command settles it.\n\n## 6. Triage every incident: instrument it, refuse on it, or record it\n\n\"Prefer the instrument over the caveat\" is only half a rule \u2014 it applies when the failure is **instrumentable**. There\nare three dispositions, not two, and they are distinguishable in practice:\n\n| disposition | when it applies | examples from one afternoon |\n|---|---|---|\n| **1. Instrument it** | the failure can be made to *not happen that way* | fixture hashes instead of a count comparison; a byte comparison instead of a grep; the guard on the path instead of in a drawer; four documented exit labels instead of an undocumented third state |\n| **2. Refuse on it** | the failure is **structural** \u2014 the check cannot validate its own precondition | the missing-shim case cannot be instrumented away by more checking, so it fails closed (`UNVERIFIABLE`, exit 2); a short run refuses (`tokens != N`) because an empty artifact must never read as agreement |\n| **3. Record it** | the failure is a property of the **world**, not of the instrument | the decode rate moves with load; the churn moves with the comgr cache state; the embedded AXLF metadata carries no toolchain, so `toolchain: null` *is* the answer \u2014 these stay as facts **with their parameters attached** (n, conditions, ref, precision) |\n\n**So the operative question after each incident is not \"instrument or document\" but: can this move from 3 to 1 or 2?**\nTwo clauses keep that actionable rather than aspirational:\n\n- **3 alone is not an acceptable resting place for a failure that can silently yield a wrong result.** It has to become\n  1, or it has to become 2. A recorded *fact* is fine; a recorded *risk* is not.\n- **The check on over-applying the rule:** you cannot instrument the absence of your own instrument. When the\n  precondition of the check is what failed, refusing **is** the instrument \u2014 which is why `UNVERIFIABLE` is a verdict\n  and not an apology.\n\n**The metric that keeps this honest, and it is a question rather than a practice:** *can this check pass by accident?*\nA check that *can* \u2014 one that a pattern, a stale value, an empty run or a missing artifact could satisfy for the wrong\nreason \u2014 is disposition-1 material by definition. The byte comparison was preferred over the grep for exactly this\nreason: it is the first verification in the session that could not have passed by pattern accident.\n\n### Worked case: a disposition-1 fix for a disposition-3 fact\n\nApplying the metric to the guard itself: `ADMISSIBLE` certified the sampling **input** \u2014 which values, drawn from what\nstate \u2014 and *nothing* said that output equality does not follow. Two ADMISSIBLE runs can still produce different\ntokens, because the residual nondeterminism is compute-side (#2213 is the standing proof). The mechanism was honest;\nthe **label invited an inference one notch stronger than its scope**, and a reader who took ADMISSIBLE for \"this run\nis reproducible\" was accidentally served.\n\nThe repair splits by disposition, which is the point of rule 6:\n\n- **the inference is disposition 1** \u2014 every ADMISSIBLE label in both guards now carries\n  `(input certified; output equality NOT implied \u2014 #2213)`, and the fixture header opens with a SCOPE block;\n- **the fact stays disposition 3** \u2014 token equality cannot become a gate (measured flaky: 5/6 uncontended, 3/4\n  concurrent, 0/6 on a quiet box in another sample) and must not become a refusal (refusing a legitimate run would be\n  wrong), so it is recorded with its rate and conditions.\n\n**You cannot instrument the fact, but you can stop the label from implying it.** That distinction \u2014 fixable inference,\nrecorded fact \u2014 is the general shape of every scope correction in this document.\n\n### Anchoring is a habit, not knowledge\n\nBoth agents hit the same substring phantom on the same day, the second *while holding the rule that forbids it*:\n`ADMISSIBLE\\[` unanchored matches **inside** `INADMISSIBLE[` (four labels mis-classified as passing verdicts until\nanchored), and `rand_calls=` matches inside `srand_calls=`. So the trap fires as reliably against someone who knows\nabout it as against someone who has never heard of it \u2014 which is the same argument as byte comparison over `-i`, and\nthe reason these belong in the instrument rather than in a reader's memory.\n\n\n**A fourth instance closes the argument, and it is mine.** Verifying that scope clause's coverage, I keyed the check on\n`^\\s*v=\"ADMISSIBLE` \u2014 which *under*-counted, because one verdict is assigned after `then `, so the anchor missed it and\nreported 2 of 3 compliant when all three were. The structural key that worked (3/3, and immune to the phantom) is **the\nexit code**: every site that exits `0` is an admissible verdict and must carry the scope clause. Where a script\n*assigns* a verdict and prints it later, the structural key is unavailable, and the fallback is a **word-boundary**\npattern (`(^|[^A-Z])ADMISSIBLE \\[`) \u2014 which has its own blind spot (it excluded the hyphenated `ADMISSIBLE-as-post`,\ncaught only by the exit-code key). So the ordering is:\n\n**bytes > structure (exit codes, presence, counts) > word-boundary pattern > bare substring** \u2014 and only the first two\nare safe to trust without reading the matched lines. Four mis-classifications in one night came from the last level,\nand a fifth from the third.\n\n**A structural key is safe against phantoms, not against a differently-shaped sibling.** The exit-code key \u2014 *every\nsite that exits 0 is an admissible verdict and must carry the clause* \u2014 was exactly right for `guard_fixture.sh` and\nexactly wrong for `guard_v4.sh`, whose fail-closed `UNVERIFIABLE` branch exited **0**, and which simply *ended* at its\n`printf`, so its exit status was the printf's: **0 for every verdict, including `INADMISSIBLE`**. Removing Lemonade strands these.\n- The `*-HRX` recipes (Lemonade already rides HRX).\n\n### D3 \u2014 Lemonade loses (authority, not code)\n- **Registry authority** \u2014 no registry of record in\n  `~/.cache/lemonade/config.json` / `user_models.json` / recipes.\n- **Routing authority** \u2014 Lemonade's `RoutingPolicyEngine` does not decide\n  model placement; the engine's router does.\n- **Model-id authority** \u2014 one canonical id scheme; recipes consume ids, they\n  do not mint them.\n\n### D4 \u2014 HRX is an acceleration lane, never the base\nPer `hrx-engine-goal.md` (fork A, reframe 2026-08-29), the original\n\"HRX *is* the engine\" end-state is **explicitly retracted by the repo's own\nassessment**:\n\n- No stable `hrx-system` userspace release (last tag May 2026; bundles ship only\n  through AMD's temporary staging channel); upstream PR #27218 still draft with\n  maintainer pushback.\n- Hard `GET_ROWS` ceiling \u2014 only K-quant-class token embeddings fuse (verified\n  across b59 and b66).\n- b66 cannot read `block_q4nx` at all; HRX2 (dev build) can. So \"a backend can serve this artifact\" must never be read as\n\"this backend should be preferred\": the quality gate is a **separate field**, never\nfolded into capability.\n\n### D5c \u2014 `HRX-GGUF` and `HRX2-GGUF-Q4NX` must never share a backend\nThird objection. dtype 42 means three different things to three readers (F5), so\nhanding a `*-q4nx.gguf` to the mainline HRX path yields **garbage rather than an error**.\nThe bridge must **refuse** to translate `HRX2-GGUF-Q4NX` until a backend advertises it,\nnot map it onto `HRX_GPU`.\n\n### D5 \u2014 Vulkan/RADV is the commodity lane, never the moat lane\n- RADV beats HRX2 on identical Qwen3-0.6B Q4_K: **+21% prefill / +53.5% decode**;\n  the decode gap is launch/codegen structure (dot2/coopmat knobs are flat), the\n  prefill gap is coopmat.\n- RADV exposes the **only coopmat lane on gfx1151** (there is no WMMA ISA on\n  this part \u2014 the probe is conclusive).\n- **But no Vulkan shaders exist for the moat ops**: Q4NX/type42, zaya/CCA\n  recurrent graph, loom routes, TQ2 ternary.\n- And the moat is gated on the **numeric contract**, not on speed: engine float\n  reference corr 1.000000 through depth 26 / 0.999995+ at 38 with exact MoE\n  routing, vs NPU/HRX int8 kernels at 0.9985\u20130.9996 per layer. It\n  already parses configs and fills `ModelConfig`; the #1831 follow-up\n  (v4-header/arch-enum modernization) is the natural vehicle.\n- **R3 \u2014 Format-driven placement.** 1BP/Q4NX \u2192 NPU (`rt_HRX`) or HIP;\n  GGUF/K-quant-embedding \u2192 HRX when the graph fits, else RADV; MLX group-affine\n  \u2192 LSE; everything else \u2192 CPU. A recipe must never be the only path to a model.\n- **R7 \u2014 `/v1/models` = registry state**, in the engine's own serving mode.\n  **Correction (2026-09-10, from a live probe of the production server):** R7 is\n  **NOT yet satisfied under `--lemonade`**. `tools/unified_server.cpp:1224-1225`\n  returns `run_embedded_lemonade(argc, argv)` immediately when `--lemonade` is\n  present, *before* any of the engine's own routes are registered. So in that\n  mode the engine's `/v1/models` enrichment never runs and `/v1/registry` is a\n  **404** \u2014 the compat face belongs entirely to Lemonade's server core. The sentinel states this in-band so a green listing cannot be read as\n  execution.\n- **R8 \u2014 Lemonade and FLM are executors behind the resolver**, so the moat\n  formats stop being invisible behind a GGUF-gated recipe catalog.\n\n### Step 2c-2 FLIP DECISION: do NOT flip wholesale \u2014 flip per lane\n`1bit route-compare` (onebin subcommand, `tools/route_compare.cpp`) prints what ships\ntoday (`select_backend_route`, the architecture-keyed static table) beside what the\nregistry resolver would pick, per file. **Measured on the live strixhalo store:\n`same=0 differs=5 registry-unknown=0`.**\n\n| file | router (shipped) | registry | what the measurement says |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `Qwen3-0.6B-Q4_K_M.gguf` | `hrx_gpu > ggml_vulkan > zinc_gpu > cpu` | `ggml_vulkan > cpu` | router leads with HRX; **measured FAIL** (q6_K embedding) |\n| **`Coder-30B-A3B-Q4_K_M.gguf`** | `hrx_gpu > ggml_vulkan > zinc_gpu > cpu` | **`hrx_gpu`** > ggml_vulkan > hip_gpu > cpu | **both lead with HRX, and this is the ONE measured-PASS class** |\n| `zaya-Q4_K.gguf` | `hrx_gpu > ggml_vulkan > zinc_gpu > cpu` | `ggml_vulkan > hip_gpu > cpu` | router leads with HRX; **measured FAIL** (arch unknown) |\n| `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Q8_0.gguf` | `cpu_qwen3_5 > hip_gpu > cpu` | `ggml_vulkan > hip_gpu > cpu` | router has a **class-specific CPU backend the registry cannot express** |\n| `zaya1-8b.q4nx` | `hip_gpu > cpu` | `fused_gpu_npu > hip_1bp_gpu > vulkan_hpp_gpu > npu_flm` | router does **not** take the ONEBP chain for a native `.q4nx` |\n\n**Reading.** (1) Where reality is known \u2014 the one class measured to pass on HRX \u2014 the two\n**agree on the head**. That directly answers the\n\"registry is poorer than the router\" finding \u2014 a flip loses no route the engine has today \u2014\nand it makes the flip one line in `backend_manager`. Measured effect, per file:\n\n| file | router head | merged head | lanes preserved |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `Coder-30B-A3B` (**measured PASS**) | `hrx_gpu` | **`hrx_gpu` \u2014 unchanged** | `zinc_gpu` kept |\n| `Qwen3-0.6B-Q4_K_M` (measured FAIL) | `hrx_gpu` | `ggml_vulkan` | `hrx_gpu` demoted, not dropped |\n| `zaya-Q4_K` (measured FAIL) | `hrx_gpu` | `ggml_vulkan` | `hrx_gpu`, `zinc_gpu` kept |\n| `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Q8_0` | `cpu_qwen3_5` | `ggml_vulkan` | **`cpu_qwen3_5` kept at the tail** |\n| `zaya1-8b.q4nx` | `hip_gpu` | `npu_flm` | `hip_gpu` kept |\n\n**The one measured-PASS class keeps its head**, the measured-FAIL classes lose the HRX\nhead, and **no lane is ever removed**. **FLIPPED 2026-09-10 (`d0b84ac1c`)**:\n`select_route_with_registry()` in `model_registry_route.cpp` packages the merge, and\n`tools/unified_server.cpp` now calls it at all three serving entry points (initial init +\nboth model-switch paths), so the resolver is consumed by the serving path rather than merely\navailable to it. `1bit registry-merge-invariants` was extended to assert the flip itself as\n**INV-3** (the packaged call must equal the primitive; a null registry must return the router\nroute unchanged) and passes on the live store: **`checked=19 INV-1=0 INV-2=0 INV-3=0`, exit 0**.\nThe live `route-compare` at that head reproduces this section's direction: measured-PASS\n30B-A3B keeps `hrx_gpu` (+`hip_gpu`), 0.6B-Q4_K_M moves `hrx_gpu`\u2192`ggml_vulkan` (no lane\nlost), and `zaya1-8b.q4nx` keeps `hip_gpu` (+`npu_flm`).\n\n**THE MERGE DEFERS UNLESS THERE IS A STATED EXCLUSION** (`7a6778728`) \u2014 and this corrected\nmy own first version, which put the registry's order first **unconditionally**.
